  543. <h3>Wire it up (no surprises)</h3>
  544. <ol>
  545. <li><p><strong>Add repos to infra core Kustomization:</strong> append the four new <code>helmrepo-*.yaml</code> files to
  546. <code>gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/kustomization.yaml</code> (see the “kustomization-additions.yaml” note in canvas).</p>
  547. </li>
  548. <li><p><strong>Tell Flux to reconcile these apps:</strong> append the seven app dirs to
  549. <code>gitops/apps/kustomization.yaml</code> (also shown in the canvas note).</p>
  550. </li>
  551. <li><p><strong>Secrets → SOPS:</strong> replace the placeholder values in:</p>
  552. <ul>
  553. <li><code>gitops/apps/minio/secret-root.yaml</code></li>
  554. <li><code>gitops/apps/mimir/secret-s3.yaml</code>
  555. and encrypt them with your existing <code>.sops.yaml</code> process.</li>
  556. </ul>
  557. </li>
  558. <li><p><strong>Commit &amp; push:</strong> Flux will bring them up in order (MinIO → Mimir/Loki/Tempo → kube-prom-stack → Alloy/DCGM).</p>
  559. </li>
  560. </ol>
  561. <p>Want me to also add an example <strong>Grafana Ingress</strong>, <strong>MinIO TLS</strong>, or a <strong>GPU temp alert</strong> (PrometheusRule) following your <code>git-local</code> issuer pattern?</p>
  562. <hr>
  563. <p>You’ve got two blockers:</p>
  564. <ol>
  565. <li><strong>Bad NVIDIA Helm repo URL</strong> → Flux can’t fetch it, so the whole <code>apps</code> Kustomization never becomes “Ready.”</li>
  566. <li><strong>A small Kustomize schema typo</strong> in <code>gitops/apps/mimir/kustomization.yaml</code> (missing <code>apiVersion</code>).</li>
  567. </ol>
  568. <p>Fix these and it’ll reconcile.</p>
  569. <h1>1) Replace the NVIDIA Helm repo</h1>
  570. <p>NVIDIA’s DCGM Exporter charts are served from <strong>gpu-helm-charts</strong>, not <code>gpu-helm-charts</code> at <code>nvidia.github.io/gpu-helm-charts</code> (that 404s). Use either of NVIDIA’s official URLs:</p>
  571. <ul>
  572. <li><code>https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/helm-charts</code> (DCGM Exporter site), or</li>
  573. <li><code>https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-monitoring-tools/helm-charts</code> (same repo via toolkit site). (<a href="https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/" title="Helm charts for GPU metrics | dcgm-exporter">NVIDIA GitHub</a>)</li>
  574. </ul>
  575. <h3>Patch</h3>
  576. <p><strong><code>gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/helmrepo-nvidia.yaml</code></strong></p>
  577. <pre><code class="language-yaml">apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
  578. kind: HelmRepository
  579. metadata:
  580. name: dcgm-exporter # was: nvidia
  581. namespace: flux-system
  582. spec:
  583. interval: 30m
  584. url: https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/helm-charts
  585. </code></pre>
  586. <p><strong><code>gitops/apps/dcgm-exporter/release.yaml</code></strong> (point to the new repo name)</p>
  587. <pre><code class="language-yaml">spec:
  588. chart:
  589. spec:
  590. chart: dcgm-exporter
  591. sourceRef:
  592. kind: HelmRepository
  593. name: dcgm-exporter # was: nvidia
  594. namespace: flux-system
  595. </code></pre>
  596. <blockquote>
  597. <p>Optional: if you prefer the toolkit URL, swap the repo URL to
  598. <code>https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-monitoring-tools/helm-charts</code>. (<a href="https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-monitoring-tools/" title="Helm charts for GPU metrics | gpu-monitoring-tools">NVIDIA GitHub</a>)</p>
  599. </blockquote>
  600. <h1>2) Add the missing apiVersion to Mimir’s Kustomization</h1>
  601. <p><strong><code>gitops/apps/mimir/kustomization.yaml</code></strong></p>
  602. <pre><code class="language-yaml">apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1 # ← add this line
  603. kind: Kustomization
  604. resources:
  605. - namespace.yaml
  606. - secret-s3.yaml
  607. - release.yaml

  609. <h1>3) (Sanity) Avoid committing real creds</h1>
  610. <p>I noticed <code>loki/release.yaml</code> and <code>tempo/release.yaml</code> have literal <code>accessKeyId/secretAccessKey</code>. Swap these to use the same SOPS-managed MinIO creds you already created (or reference a Secret) to avoid leaking secrets in Git.</p>
  611. <p>Example for Loki:</p>
  612. <pre><code class="language-yaml">values:
  613. loki:
  614. storage:
  615. s3:
  616. accessKeyId: ${MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID} # from a Secret or valuesFrom
  617. secretAccessKey: ${MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}
  618. </code></pre>
  619. <h1>4) Reconcile in the right order</h1>
  620. <pre><code class="language-bash"># 4a) Apply your commit, then force the sources/Kustomizations to refresh:
  621. flux reconcile source git platform-config -n flux-system
  622. ​
  623. # 4b) Make sure Helm repos are healthy now:
  624. flux get sources helm -n flux-system
  625. # Expect OK for: grafana, prometheus-community, bitnami, gpu-helm-charts
  626. ​
  627. # 4c) If &#39;apps&#39; is still suspended for any reason, resume and watch:
  628. flux resume kustomization apps -n flux-system
  629. flux get kustomizations -A
  630. ​
  631. # 4d) Nudge infra core first (repos), then apps:
  632. flux reconcile kustomization infra-core -n flux-system
  633. flux reconcile kustomization apps -n flux-system
  634. ​
  635. # 4e) Tail logs if anything flaps:
  636. flux logs -n flux-system --since=15m
  637. </code></pre>
  638. <h1>5) Quick health checklist</h1>
  639. <ul>
  640. <li><code>kubectl -n flux-system describe helmrepository gpu-helm-charts</code> → should show a fetched index, not 404. (<a href="https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/" title="Helm charts for GPU metrics | dcgm-exporter">NVIDIA GitHub</a>)</li>
  641. <li><code>kubectl -n monitoring get helmrelease</code> → <code>kube-prometheus-stack</code>, <code>alloy</code>, <code>dcgm-exporter</code> should go <code>Succeeded</code>.</li>
  642. <li><code>kubectl -n mimir get svc</code> → <code>mimir-nginx</code> present.</li>
  643. <li><code>kubectl -n loki get svc</code> → <code>loki-gateway</code> present.</li>
  644. <li><code>kubectl -n monitoring get svc</code> → <code>alloy-otlp</code> present.</li>
  645. </ul>
  646. <p>If you want, I can also push a quick commit-ready patch that:</p>
  647. <ul>
  648. <li>swaps DCGM repo + fixes Mimir kustomization,</li>
  649. <li>moves MinIO creds for Loki/Tempo into Secrets (SOPS-ready),</li>
  650. <li>and adds tiny NetPols to mirror your existing style.</li>
  651. </ul>
  652. <hr>
  653. <p>Yep — you can (and should) stop hard-coding the MinIO creds in Loki/Tempo. The clean, chart-supported way is:</p>
  654. <ol>
  655. <li><strong>Put the creds in per-namespace Secrets</strong> (K8s can’t mount a Secret across namespaces),</li>
  656. <li><strong>Inject them as env vars</strong> into Loki/Tempo pods, and</li>
  657. <li><strong>expand env vars in their configs</strong> so <code>${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}</code> / <code>${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}</code> are used instead of literals.</li>
  658. </ol>
  659. <p>Below are drop-in diffs + files to do exactly that, and one fix for your NVIDIA Helm repo that’s currently 404’ing (it’s what’s making <code>flux resume …</code> sit there).</p>
  660. <hr>
  661. <h1>Patches</h1>
  662. <h3>1) Fix the bad NVIDIA Helm repo URL (prevents reconciliation hang)</h3>
  663. <p>The correct repo for <strong>dcgm-exporter</strong> is:</p>
  664. <ul>
  665. <li><code>https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/helm-charts</code> (not <code>https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-helm-charts</code>). (<a href="https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/" title="Helm charts for GPU metrics | dcgm-exporter">GitHub</a>, <a href="https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-monitoring-tools/" title="Helm charts for GPU metrics | gpu-monitoring-tools">NVIDIA Docs</a>)</li>
  666. </ul>
  667. <pre><code class="language-diff">diff --git a/gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/helmrepo-nvidia.yaml b/gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/helmrepo-nvidia.yaml
  668. @@
  669. spec:
  670. interval: 30m
  671. - url: https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-helm-charts
  672. + url: https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/helm-charts
  673. </code></pre>
  674. <blockquote>
  675. <p>After committing this, Flux will be able to fetch the index for <code>dcgm-exporter</code> and continue.</p>
  676. </blockquote>
  677. <hr>
  678. <h3>2) Loki — use env vars from a Secret (+ enable env expansion)</h3>
  679. <p>The Loki chart supports <code>global.extraEnvFrom</code> and <code>global.extraArgs</code> (use <code>-config.expand-env=true</code>) so you can reference <code>${…}</code> in the storage config. (<a href="https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/setup/install/helm/reference/" title="Helm chart values | Grafana Loki documentation
  680. ">Grafana Labs</a>)</p>
  681. <p><strong>Create a Secret in the <code>loki</code> namespace</strong> (see file below), then patch the HelmRelease:</p>
  682. <pre><code class="language-diff">diff --git a/gitops/apps/loki/release.yaml b/gitops/apps/loki/release.yaml
  683. @@
  684. spec:
  685. interval: 30m
  686. @@
  687. values:
  688. + global:
  689. + extraArgs:
  690. + - &quot;-config.expand-env=true&quot;
  691. + extraEnvFrom:
  692. + - secretRef:
  693. + name: loki-s3
  694. loki:
  695. commonConfig:
  696. replication_factor: 1
  697. storage:
  698. type: s3
  699. s3:
  700. s3ForcePathStyle: true
  701. endpoint: http://minio.minio.svc.cluster.local:9000
  702. insecure: true
  703. bucketnames:
  704. chunks: loki-chunks
  705. ruler: loki-ruler
  706. admin: loki-admin
  707. - accessKeyId: &quot;core-admin&quot;
  708. - secretAccessKey: &quot;OhGhah7ahto0lax&quot;
  709. + accessKeyId: &quot;${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}&quot;
  710. + secretAccessKey: &quot;${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}&quot;
  711. gateway:
  712. enabled: true
  713. serviceMonitor:
  714. enabled: true
  715. </code></pre>
  716. <p>Add the Secret to the kustomization:</p>
  717. <pre><code class="language-diff">diff --git a/gitops/apps/loki/kustomization.yaml b/gitops/apps/loki/kustomization.yaml
  718. @@
  719. resources:
  720. - namespace.yaml
  721. + - secret-s3.yaml
  722. - release.yaml
  723. </code></pre>
  724. <p><strong>New file:</strong> <code>gitops/apps/loki/secret-s3.yaml</code></p>
  725. <pre><code class="language-yaml">apiVersion: v1
  726. kind: Secret
  727. metadata:
  728. name: loki-s3
  729. namespace: loki
  730. type: Opaque
  731. stringData:
  732. # Use the same values as your MinIO root secret
  733. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: &quot;CHANGE_ME_MINIO_ROOT_USER&quot;
  734. AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: &quot;CHANGE_ME_MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD&quot;
  735. </code></pre>
  736. <blockquote>
  737. <p>Why this works: with <code>-config.expand-env=true</code>, Loki expands <code>${…}</code> in its config; the Helm chart lets us inject env from a Secret (<code>global.extraEnvFrom</code>). (<a href="https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/setup/install/helm/reference/" title="Helm chart values | Grafana Loki documentation
  738. ">Grafana Labs</a>)</p>
  739. </blockquote>
  740. <hr>
  741. <h3>3) Tempo — use env vars from a Secret (+ enable env expansion)</h3>
  742. <p>The <strong>tempo</strong> chart exposes <code>tempo.extraEnvFrom</code> / <code>tempo.extraEnv</code> and supports <code>tempo.extraArgs</code> (including <code>-config.expand-env=true</code>). (<a href="https://artifacthub.io/packages/helm/grafana/tempo/1.0.0?utm_source=chatgpt.com" title="tempo 1.0.0 - Grafana">Artifact Hub</a>, <a href="https://grafana.com/docs/tempo/latest/setup/helm-chart/?utm_source=chatgpt.com" title="Deploy Tempo with Helm">Grafana Labs</a>, <a href="https://community.grafana.com/t/azure-storage-configuration-for-tempo-distributed/110125?utm_source=chatgpt.com" title="Azure Storage configuration for Tempo Distributed">Grafana Labs Community Forums</a>)
  743. Tempo’s S3 client will read access keys from env once you reference <code>${…}</code> in the config (or omit and let SDK pick them up). (<a href="https://grafana.com/docs/tempo/latest/configuration/hosted-storage/s3/?utm_source=chatgpt.com" title="Amazon S3 permissions | Grafana Tempo documentation">Grafana Labs</a>)</p>
  744. <pre><code class="language-diff">diff --git a/gitops/apps/tempo/release.yaml b/gitops/apps/tempo/release.yaml
  745. @@
  746. values:
  747. - tempo:
  748. + tempo:
  749. + extraArgs:
  750. + - &quot;-config.expand-env=true&quot;
  751. + extraEnvFrom:
  752. + - secretRef:
  753. + name: tempo-s3
  754. server:
  755. http_listen_port: 3200
  756. storage:
  757. trace:
  758. backend: s3
  759. s3:
  760. endpoint: minio.minio.svc.cluster.local:9000
  761. insecure: true
  762. bucket: tempo
  763. - access_key: &quot;core-admin&quot;
  764. - secret_key: &quot;OhGhah7ahto0lax&quot;
  765. + access_key: &quot;${AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID}&quot;
  766. + secret_key: &quot;${AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}&quot;
  767. metricsGenerator:
  768. enabled: true
  769. remoteWriteUrl: http://mimir-nginx.mimir.svc.cluster.local/api/v1/push
  770. serviceMonitor:
  771. enabled: true
  772. </code></pre>
  773. <p>Add the Secret to the kustomization:</p>
  774. <pre><code class="language-diff">diff --git a/gitops/apps/tempo/kustomization.yaml b/gitops/apps/tempo/kustomization.yaml
  775. @@
  776. resources:
  777. - namespace.yaml
  778. + - secret-s3.yaml
  779. - release.yaml
  780. </code></pre>
  781. <p><strong>New file:</strong> <code>gitops/apps/tempo/secret-s3.yaml</code></p>
  782. <pre><code class="language-yaml">apiVersion: v1
  783. kind: Secret
  784. metadata:
  785. name: tempo-s3
  786. namespace: tempo
  787. type: Opaque
  788. stringData:
  789. AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: &quot;CHANGE_ME_MINIO_ROOT_USER&quot;
  790. AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: &quot;CHANGE_ME_MINIO_ROOT_PASSWORD&quot;
  791. </code></pre>
  792. <hr>
  793. <h1>About reusing your SOPS-encrypted MinIO secret</h1>
  794. <ul>
  795. <li><p><strong>Direct reuse across namespaces isn’t possible.</strong> K8s doesn’t allow mounting a Secret from another namespace. You need <strong>one Secret per namespace</strong> that consumes it (here: <code>loki</code> and <code>tempo</code>).</p>
  796. </li>
  797. <li><p><strong>Two quick ways to stay SOPS-native:</strong></p>
  798. <ol>
  799. <li><p><strong>Copy the values</strong> from your <code>minio/minio-root</code> secret into the new <code>loki-s3</code> and <code>tempo-s3</code> Secret files and run:</p>
  800. <pre><code class="language-bash">sops -e -i gitops/apps/loki/secret-s3.yaml
  801. sops -e -i gitops/apps/tempo/secret-s3.yaml
  802. </code></pre>
  803. <p>This re-encrypts and writes the SOPS metadata/MAC correctly.</p>
  804. </li>
  805. <li><p>If you want zero duplication long-term, switch to <strong>KSOPS (kustomize SOPS plugin)</strong> or <strong>External Secrets Operator</strong> so you can source one encrypted secret and fan it out per namespace at render time. (Happy to wire that up next.)</p>
  806. </li>
  807. </ol>
  808. </li>
  809. </ul>
  810. <hr>
  811. <h1>Why your Flux apply was “hanging”</h1>
  812. <p>Your logs show repeated failures fetching the NVIDIA repo (<code>404 Not Found</code>), which blocks the relevant HelmRepository becoming <strong>Ready</strong>. Fixing the URL above resolves that bottleneck and lets the <code>apps</code> Kustomization reconcile again. (<a href="https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-monitoring-tools/" title="Helm charts for GPU metrics | gpu-monitoring-tools">NVIDIA Docs</a>)</p>
  813. <hr>
  814. <p>If you want, I can also:</p>
  815. <ul>
  816. <li>strip the <strong>access_key/secret_key</strong> lines entirely from Tempo and rely on the AWS SDK env lookup,</li>
  817. <li>add a tiny <strong><code>Secret</code> template</strong> you can reuse (name + namespace as params), or</li>
  818. <li>switch to <strong>KSOPS</strong> so you define the secret once and generate it in both namespaces at build time.</li>
  819. </ul>
  820. <p>Which do you prefer?</p>
  821. <hr>
  822. <p>Yep — your NVIDIA repo error is because we pointed at a URL that doesn’t exist. The right URLs today are:</p>
  823. <ul>
  824. <li><strong>DCGM Exporter Helm repo</strong> (stand-alone metrics): <code>https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/helm-charts</code>. (<a href="https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/" title="Helm charts for GPU metrics | dcgm-exporter">NVIDIA GitHub</a>, <a href="https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-monitoring-tools/" title="Helm charts for GPU metrics | gpu-monitoring-tools">GitHub</a>)</li>
  825. <li><strong>GPU Operator Helm repo</strong> (drivers + device plugin + optional DCGM Exporter): <code>https://nvidia.github.io/gpu-operator</code>. (<a href="https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/setup/install/helm/reference/" title="Helm chart values | Grafana Loki documentation
  826. ">NVIDIA GitHub</a>)</li>
  827. </ul>
  828. <p>Notes:</p>
  829. <ul>
  830. <li>NVIDIA also documents an <strong>NGC</strong> Helm repo (<code>https://helm.ngc.nvidia.com/nvidia</code>), but folks occasionally hit 403s from it; the GitHub Pages repo above is fine for public installs. (<a href="https://artifacthub.io/packages/helm/grafana/tempo/1.0.0?utm_source=chatgpt.com" title="tempo 1.0.0 - Grafana">NVIDIA Docs</a>, <a href="https://grafana.com/docs/tempo/latest/setup/helm-chart/?utm_source=chatgpt.com" title="Deploy Tempo with Helm">Discuss Kubernetes</a>)</li>
  831. <li>If you install the <strong>GPU Operator</strong>, it <strong>deploys DCGM Exporter for you</strong>; don’t also install the stand-alone dcgm-exporter chart or you’ll get duplicate metrics. (<a href="https://community.grafana.com/t/azure-storage-configuration-for-tempo-distributed/110125?utm_source=chatgpt.com" title="Azure Storage configuration for Tempo Distributed">NVIDIA Docs</a>)</li>
  832. </ul>
  833. <hr>
  834. <h2>Minimal fix (keep <strong>stand-alone dcgm-exporter</strong> only)</h2>
  835. <ol>
  836. <li>Replace your broken repo with a dedicated DCGM Exporter repo.</li>
  837. </ol>
  838. <p><strong>gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/helmrepo-nvidia.yaml → helmrepo-dcgm-exporter.yaml</strong></p>
  839. <pre><code class="language-yaml">apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
  840. kind: HelmRepository
  841. metadata:
  842. name: dcgm-exporter
  843. namespace: flux-system
  844. spec:
  845. interval: 30m
  846. url: https://nvidia.github.io/dcgm-exporter/helm-charts
  847. </code></pre>
  848. <p>…and add this filename to <code>gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/kustomization.yaml</code> (and remove the old <code>helmrepo-nvidia.yaml</code> entry).</p>
  849. <ol start="2">
  850. <li>Point your HelmRelease at the new repo name.</li>
  851. </ol>
  852. <p><strong>gitops/apps/dcgm-exporter/release.yaml</strong></p>
  853. <pre><code class="language-diff"> spec:
  854. interval: 30m
  855. chart:
  856. spec:
  857. chart: dcgm-exporter
  858. sourceRef:
  859. kind: HelmRepository
  860. - name: nvidia
  861. + name: dcgm-exporter
  862. namespace: flux-system
  863. </code></pre>
  864. <p>That’s it for the error you’re seeing. After pushing, you can force Flux to settle:</p>
  865. <pre><code class="language-bash">flux reconcile source helm dcgm-exporter -n flux-system
  866. flux reconcile kustomization infra-core -n flux-system
  867. flux reconcile kustomization apps -n flux-system
  868. </code></pre>
  869. <p>Check it’s green:</p>
  870. <pre><code class="language-bash">flux get sources helm -A
  871. flux get helmreleases -A | grep dcgm

  873. <hr>
  874. <h2>Alternative: switch to <strong>GPU Operator</strong> (and drop stand-alone dcgm-exporter)</h2>
  875. <p>If you want the operator to manage drivers, device plugin, runtime, MIG, <strong>and</strong> expose GPU metrics via DCGM Exporter, add this repo:</p>

  888. <p>Then create the release (example with defaults; set <code>driver.enabled=false</code> if you already have host drivers):</p>
  889. <p><strong>gitops/apps/gpu-operator/release.yaml</strong></p>
  890. <pre><code class="language-yaml">apiVersion: helm.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v2
  891. kind: HelmRelease
  892. metadata:
  893. name: gpu-operator
  894. namespace: gpu-operator
  895. spec:
  896. interval: 30m
  897. chart:
  898. spec:
  899. chart: gpu-operator
  900. sourceRef:
  901. kind: HelmRepository
  902. name: nvidia-gpu-operator
  903. namespace: flux-system
  904. values:
  905. # flip to false if you already manage drivers on the host

  907. enabled: true

  909. <p>Add <code>gitops/apps/gpu-operator/</code> to <code>gitops/apps/kustomization.yaml</code> and <strong>remove</strong> the <code>gitops/apps/dcgm-exporter/</code> entry to avoid double scraping. The operator includes DCGM Exporter for Prometheus. (<a href="https://community.grafana.com/t/azure-storage-configuration-for-tempo-distributed/110125?utm_source=chatgpt.com" title="Azure Storage configuration for Tempo Distributed">NVIDIA Docs</a>)</p>
  910. <hr>
  911. <h2>About your MinIO creds</h2>
  912. <p>You asked earlier about removing literals from Loki/Tempo — yes, keep using the <strong>SOPS-encrypted</strong> <code>minio-root</code> secret you already have and reference it via <code>envFrom.secretRef</code> or chart values that accept existing secrets (we already patched the manifests that way).</p>
  913. <hr>
  914. <p>If you want, I can spit out the exact diffs to (a) swap in <strong>dcgm-exporter</strong> only, or (b) migrate fully to <strong>GPU Operator</strong> and delete the stand-alone exporter. Which route do you want to take?</p>
  915. <hr>
  916. <p>Good news: the error in your logs points to one concrete issue + one likely config gotcha.</p>
  917. <h2>What’s breaking reconciliation</h2>
  918. <ul>
  919. <li><p><strong>infra-core Kustomization still references <code>helmrepo-nvidia.yaml</code></strong>, but you removed/renamed that file. Kustomize can’t find it:</p>
  920. <pre><code>accumulating resources from &#39;helmrepo-nvidia.yaml&#39;: ... no such file or directory
  921. </code></pre>
  922. </li>
  923. <li><p><strong><code>apps</code> is still suspended</strong> (or being re-suspended by Git). Your logs show:</p>
  924. <pre><code>Kustomization/apps.flux-system - Reconciliation is suspended for this object
  925. </code></pre>
  926. <p>If <code>cluster-root</code> keeps applying a manifest with <code>spec.suspend: true</code>, <code>flux resume</code> will appear to work and then get undone on the next reconcile.</p>
  927. </li>
  928. </ul>
  929. <hr>
  930. <h2>Fix it fast (exact edits)</h2>
  931. <h3>1) Remove the stale file reference from infra-core</h3>
  932. <p>Edit <code>gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/kustomization.yaml</code> and:</p>
  933. <ul>
  934. <li><strong>Delete</strong> the line that mentions <code>helmrepo-nvidia.yaml</code></li>
  935. <li><strong>Add</strong> the correct repo file you decided to use</li>
  936. </ul>
  937. <p>If you’re using stand-alone <strong>dcgm-exporter</strong>:</p>
  938. <pre><code class="language-diff"> resources:
  939. - helmrepo-gitea.yaml
  940. - helmrepo-local-oci.yaml
  941. - gitrepo-helm-actions.yaml
  942. - helmrepo-grafana.yaml
  943. - helmrepo-prometheus-community.yaml
  944. - helmrepo-bitnami.yaml
  945. - - helmrepo-nvidia.yaml
  946. + - helmrepo-dcgm-exporter.yaml
  947. </code></pre>
  948. <p><strong>And ensure this file exists:</strong> <code>gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/helmrepo-dcgm-exporter.yaml</code></p>
  949. <pre><code class="language-yaml">apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
  950. kind: HelmRepository
  951. metadata:
  952. name: dcgm-exporter
  953. namespace: flux-system
  954. spec:
  955. interval: 30m

  1202. <h3>Why</h3>
  1203. <p>Bitnami’s <strong>MinIO</strong> chart is now served as an <strong>OCI</strong> artifact. Your <code>HelmRepository bitnami</code> is an HTTP (index.yaml) repo, so the controller ends up trying to pull an <code>oci://…</code> URL without treating it as an OCI source — hence “unsupported protocol scheme <code>oci</code>”.</p>
  1204. <h3>Fix (recommended): add a Bitnami <strong>OCI</strong> repo and point MinIO at it</h3>
  1205. <ol>
  1206. <li>Create a separate OCI HelmRepository:</li>
  1207. </ol>
  1208. <pre><code class="language-yaml"># gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/helmrepo-bitnami-oci.yaml
  1209. apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
  1210. kind: HelmRepository
  1211. metadata:
  1212. name: bitnami-oci
  1213. namespace: flux-system
  1214. spec:
  1215. interval: 30m
  1216. type: oci
  1217. url: oci://registry-1.docker.io/bitnamicharts
  1218. </code></pre>
  1219. <ol start="2">
  1220. <li>Reference it from MinIO’s HelmRelease:</li>
  1221. </ol>
  1222. <pre><code class="language-diff"># gitops/apps/minio/release.yaml
  1223. spec:
  1224. chart:
  1225. spec:
  1226. - chart: minio
  1227. - version: &quot;^17.0.0&quot;
  1228. - sourceRef:
  1229. - kind: HelmRepository
  1230. - name: bitnami
  1231. - namespace: flux-system
  1232. + chart: minio
  1233. + version: &quot;17.0.21&quot; # keep or bump as you like
  1234. + sourceRef:
  1235. + kind: HelmRepository
  1236. + name: bitnami-oci
  1237. + namespace: flux-system
  1238. </code></pre>
  1239. <ol start="3">
  1240. <li>Include the new repo file in infra-core kustomization:</li>
  1241. </ol>
  1242. <pre><code class="language-diff"># gitops/clusters/microk8s-prod/infra/core/kustomization.yaml
  1243. resources:
  1244. - helmrepo-gitea.yaml
  1245. - helmrepo-local-oci.yaml

  1292. <p>Here&#39;s the best systematic approach to verify your monitoring flow connectivity:</p>

  1304. <pre><code class="language-bash"># Check Alloy&#39;s internal status

  1317. <pre><code class="language-bash"># Test log ingestion to Loki

  1325. ​

  1331. <pre><code class="language-bash"># Get Grafana admin password

  1502. <h3>A) Datasource UID mismatch inside the dashboard JSON</h3>
  1503. <p>Modern Grafana dashboards bind by <strong>UID</strong>, not by name. If your JSONs reference the wrong UID (e.g. from wherever you exported them), panels render but queries return “no data”.</p>

BODY=&#39;{&quot;streams&quot;:[{&quot;stream&quot;:{&quot;job&quot;:&quot;netdebug&quot;,&quot;level&quot;:&quot;info&quot;,&quot;test_id&quot;:&quot;&#39;$i&#39;&quot;},&quot;values&quot;:[[&quot;&#39;$TS&#39;&quot;,&quot;Test log entry #&#39;$i&#39; - timestamp validation successful&quot;]]}]}&#39;
  1584. STATUS=$(curl -sS -w &#39;%{http_code}&#39; -o /dev/null \

  1666. <h2>1) See the 400 error message</h2>

  1668. <pre><code class="language-bash">TS=$(date +%s%N | cut -c1-19)
  1669. BODY=&#39;{&quot;streams&quot;:[{&quot;stream&quot;:{&quot;app&quot;:&quot;direct-probe&quot;},&quot;values&quot;:[[&quot;&#39;&quot;$TS&quot;&#39;&quot;,&quot;hello from direct probe&quot;]]}]}&#39;
  1670. curl -sS -H &#39;Content-Type: application/json&#39; -H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: core&#39; \

  1674. <p>Common 400 reasons you might see:</p>
  1675. <ul>
  1676. <li><code>entry out of order</code> (timestamp older than previous ingested for the same stream)</li>
  1677. <li><code>unmarshal</code> / JSON error (rare given your body looks fine)</li>
  1678. <li><code>too far in future</code> (clock skew)</li>
  1679. <li><code>no labels</code> (you have <code>app</code>, so not this)</li>
  1680. </ul>
  1681. <p>If it says “out of order” or “too far in future”, re-push with a <strong>fresh TS</strong>:</p>
  1682. <pre><code class="language-bash">TS=$(date +%s%N); BODY=&#39;{&quot;streams&quot;:[{&quot;stream&quot;:{&quot;app&quot;:&quot;direct-probe&quot;},&quot;values&quot;:[[&quot;&#39;&quot;$TS&quot;&#39;&quot;,&quot;hi&quot;]]}]}&#39;
  1683. </code></pre>
  1684. <h2>2) Try the <strong>gateway</strong> write path (often preferred)</h2>
  1685. <p>Your Grafana datasource points at the <strong>gateway</strong>. Let’s mirror that for writes:</p>
  1686. <pre><code class="language-bash"># write via gateway
  1687. TS=$(date +%s)000000000
  1688. BODY=&#39;{&quot;streams&quot;:[{&quot;stream&quot;:{&quot;app&quot;:&quot;direct-probe&quot;},&quot;values&quot;:[[&quot;&#39;&quot;$TS&quot;&#39;&quot;,&quot;hello via gateway&quot;]]}]}&#39;
  1689. curl -sS -H &#39;Content-Type: application/json&#39; -H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: core&#39; \
  1690. -X POST --data &quot;$BODY&quot; \
  1691. http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push
  1692. ​
  1693. # read via gateway (optional)
  1694. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000
  1695. END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  1696. curl -sS -G -H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: core&#39; \
  1697. &#39;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range&#39; \
  1698. --data-urlencode &#39;query={app=&quot;direct-probe&quot;}&#39; \
  1699. --data-urlencode &quot;start=$START&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;end=$END&quot; \
  1700. --data-urlencode &quot;limit=5&quot; | jq .
  1701. </code></pre>
  1702. <h2>3) Double-check which services expose the push API</h2>
  1703. <p>Make sure we’re hitting what your chart exposes:</p>
  1704. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n loki get svc -o wide | egrep &#39;gateway|write|read&#39;
  1705. </code></pre>
  1706. <ul>
  1707. <li>For the Grafana <strong>Loki</strong> chart, <strong>gateway</strong> (NGINX) exposes <code>/loki/api/v1/push</code> and routes to the distributor.</li>
  1708. <li>The <strong>write</strong> service should also expose the push API (distributor). If it 400s while the gateway works, it’s a strong hint the request never reached the correct component (or hit some NGINX header defaults at the gateway that differ).</li>
  1709. </ul>
  1710. <h2>4) If write still 400s, check the write/distributor logs</h2>
  1711. <p>They’ll state exactly why the request was rejected:</p>
  1712. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n loki logs deploy/loki-write --tail=200 | egrep -i &#39;error|warn|push|ingest&#39;
  1713. </code></pre>
  1714. <p>(If it’s StatefulSet/DaemonSet, adjust the resource accordingly.)</p>
  1715. <h2>5) Quick tenant sanity</h2>
  1716. <p>You’re consistently using <code>X-Scope-OrgID: core</code>:</p>
  1717. <ul>
  1718. <li>Alloy writes with <code>tenant_id = &quot;core&quot;</code> ✅</li>
  1719. <li>Grafana datasource sends header <code>core</code> ✅</li>
  1720. <li>Keep the curl header as <code>core</code> ✅</li>
  1721. </ul>
  1722. <h2>6) Prometheus dashboards still empty?</h2>
  1723. <p>While we chase logs, verify Prometheus actually has samples in the last 5–10m:</p>
  1724. <pre><code class="language-bash">curl -sS &quot;http://kube-prom-prometheus.monitoring.svc.cluster.local:9090/api/v1/query&quot; \
  1725. --data-urlencode &#39;query=sum(up)&#39; | jq &#39;.data.result&#39;
  1726. </code></pre>
  1727. <p>If that’s zero/empty, panels will be blank regardless of provisioning. If it’s &gt;0, any “no data” is likely dashboard-UID mismatch or query filters too narrow.</p>
  1728. <hr>
  1729. <h3>TL;DR next actions</h3>
  1730. <ol>
  1731. <li>Run the push again <strong>and read the body</strong> to see the 400 reason.</li>

  1733. <li>If still failing, grab <strong><code>loki-write</code> logs</strong> for the error line and paste it back — that message will tell us exactly what to fix (timestamp ordering, future timestamp, etc.).</li>

  1738. <li><strong>Prometheus is scraping</strong> ( <code>sum(up)=12</code> ) so Prom dashboards should have data ✅</li>

  1776. <h2>3) Why Grafana dashboards show “No data” (despite data existing)</h2>
  1777. <p>This is typically one of these:</p>
  1778. <ul>
  1779. <li><p><strong>Datasource UID mismatch.</strong> Your provisioned UIDs are:</p>
  1780. <ul>
  1781. <li>Prometheus: <code>prometheus</code></li>
  1782. <li>Loki: <code>loki</code></li>
  1783. <li>Tempo: <code>tempo</code></li>
  1784. <li>Mimir: <code>mimir</code></li>
  1785. </ul>
  1786. <p>Make sure the JSON dashboards reference those UIDs (e.g., <code>&quot;datasource&quot;: {&quot;type&quot;:&quot;prometheus&quot;,&quot;uid&quot;:&quot;prometheus&quot;}</code> and for logs <code>&quot;uid&quot;:&quot;loki&quot;</code>). If the JSON used different UIDs (or Grafana variable like <code>${DS_PROMETHEUS}</code> that isn’t defined), panels will be blank even though Prom has data.</p>
  1787. </li>
  1788. <li><p><strong>Queries too specific for your labels.</strong> The bundled dashboards (e.g., <em>Loki Operations</em>) often look for things like <code>{job=&quot;loki-canary&quot;}</code> or particular label schemas. You don’t have the canary installed, so those panels will be empty. Try replacing with a generic query in Explore (Loki) like:</p>
  1789. <pre><code>{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;} | line_format &quot;{{pod}} {{msg}}&quot;
  1790. </code></pre>
  1791. <p>If that shows data, the dashboard panels just need tweaks to match your labels.</p>
  1792. </li>
  1793. <li><p><strong>Time range vs. scrape lag.</strong> You already queried last 10m and saw Prom data; less likely, but try 1h range once.</p>
  1794. </li>
  1795. </ul>

  1913. <p>If you want, paste one failing panel’s query, and I’ll adapt it to your label set.</p>
  1914. <p>You’re <strong>pushing fine via the gateway</strong>, but Alloy is flooding Loki with <strong>old log lines</strong>, and Loki is <strong>rejecting them</strong>:</p>
  1915. <ul>
  1916. <li><code>status=400 ... entry too far behind ... oldest acceptable timestamp is: 2025-09-12T00:11:xxZ</code>
  1917. → your Loki limits only accept ~recent entries; anything older is dropped.</li>
  1918. <li><code>status=429 ... Ingestion rate limit exceeded for user core (limit: 4194304 bytes/sec)</code>
  1919. → Alloy is replaying a <em>lot</em> of history (note the many “opened log stream … start time=1970-01-01” messages).</li>
  1920. </ul>
  1921. <p>So data-path is healthy; the problem is <strong>initial tailing position + limits</strong>.</p>
  1922. <h2>Fix (recommended: don’t backfill now)</h2>
  1923. <ol>
  1924. <li><strong>Make Alloy start at the end</strong> (only new lines):</li>
  1925. </ol>
  1926. <pre><code class="language-hcl">loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  1927. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  1928. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  1929. start_at = &quot;end&quot; # &lt;- add this
  1930. }
  1931. </code></pre>
  1932. <ol start="2">
  1933. <li><strong>Persist positions</strong> so restarts don’t re-read from the beginning. Add a writable file and point the source at it:</li>
  1934. </ol>
  1935. <pre><code class="language-hcl">local.file &quot;positions&quot; {
  1936. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  1937. }
  1938. ​
  1939. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  1940. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  1941. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  1942. start_at = &quot;end&quot;
  1943. positions = local.file.positions # &lt;- add this
  1944. }
  1945. </code></pre>
  1946. <p>…and mount a small writable dir for Alloy (e.g., EmptyDir) if the chart doesn’t already:</p>
  1947. <pre><code class="language-yaml">values:
  1948. controller:
  1949. volumes:
  1950. extra:
  1951. - name: positions
  1952. emptyDir: {}
  1953. alloy:
  1954. mounts:
  1955. extra:
  1956. - name: positions
  1957. mountPath: /tmp/alloy
  1958. </code></pre>
  1959. <ol start="3">
  1960. <li><strong>Roll Alloy</strong> to apply:</li>
  1961. </ol>
  1962. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart ds/alloy
  1963. kubectl -n monitoring rollout status ds/alloy
  1964. </code></pre>
  1965. <p>That will stop the 400/429s and you’ll see fresh logs landing (your probe via gateway already showed that queries work).</p>
  1966. <h2>If you <em>do</em> want to backfill old logs</h2>
  1967. <p>You’ll need to temporarily relax Loki limits for your tenant and raise throughput. In the Loki chart values (component that owns distributor/ingester limits):</p>
  1968. <ul>
  1969. <li><p>Increase ingestion budget (names vary by chart):</p>
  1970. <ul>
  1971. <li><code>limits_config.ingestion_rate_mb</code> and <code>limits_config.ingestion_burst_size_mb</code> (or byte/sec variants).</li>
  1972. </ul>
  1973. </li>
  1974. <li><p>Allow older entries for a while (the setting name varies by Loki version/distribution; commonly under <code>limits_config</code> something like <strong>old-entry/max-age/creation_grace_period</strong>). Set it to a window that covers the backlog (e.g., 48h), then <strong>revert</strong> after backfill.</p>
  1975. </li>
  1976. </ul>
  1977. <p>Backfilling can be noisy and expensive; the safer path is to skip it (use <code>start_at=&quot;end&quot;</code>), then rely on new data going forward.</p>

  1995. <p>If you want, I can draft the exact HelmRelease patch with <code>start_at=&quot;end&quot;</code> + positions mount for your Alloy values.</p>
  1996. <p>Good news: the errors explain exactly what broke.</p>
  1997. <h2>What the errors mean</h2>
  1998. <ol>
  1999. <li><p><strong><code>local.file &quot;positions&quot;</code> is the wrong component</strong></p>
  2000. <ul>
  2001. <li><code>local.file</code> is a <em>file reader</em> component. The Loki tailers expect a <strong>Loki positions</strong> component, not a generic file reader.</li>
  2002. <li>Hence: <em>“failed to read file … /tmp/alloy/positions.yaml: no such file”</em> during build.</li>
  2003. </ul>
  2004. </li>
  2005. <li><p><strong><code>start_at</code> isn’t a valid attribute on <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code> in your Alloy</strong></p>
  2006. <ul>
  2007. <li>You’re running <strong>grafana/alloy:v1.10.1</strong>. That version’s <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code> does <strong>not</strong> expose <code>start_at</code>. (It exists on other sources / newer versions.)</li>
  2008. <li>Hence: <em>“unrecognized attribute name <code>start_at</code>”</em>.</li>
  2009. </ul>
  2010. </li>
  2011. </ol>
  2012. <hr>
  2013. <h2>Two ways to fix</h2>
  2014. <h3>A) Quickest path (make Alloy healthy now; no backfill control)</h3>
  2015. <p>Remove the bits Alloy doesn’t understand. In your <code>values.alloy.configMap.content</code>, delete:</p>
  2016. <pre><code class="language-hcl">local.file &quot;positions&quot; {
  2017. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  2018. }
  2019. </code></pre>
  2020. <p>…and delete these attributes inside <code>loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot;</code>:</p>
  2021. <pre><code class="language-hcl">start_at = &quot;end&quot;
  2022. positions = local.file.positions
  2023. </code></pre>
  2024. <p>Then roll Alloy:</p>
  2025. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart ds/alloy
  2026. kubectl -n monitoring rollout status ds/alloy
  2027. </code></pre>
  2028. <p>Alloy will come up cleanly and keep tailing. (Old lines may still trickle until files are fully caught up, and Loki will continue to reject anything too old with 400s—this will quiet down.)</p>
  2029. <hr>
  2030. <h3>B) Proper path (control start position + persist offsets)</h3>
  2031. <ol>
  2032. <li><strong>Upgrade Alloy</strong> to a version where kubernetes source supports start position &amp; use the correct positions component. For the HelmRelease:</li>
  2033. </ol>
  2034. <pre><code class="language-yaml">values:
  2035. alloy:
  2036. image:
  2037. repository: docker.io/grafana/alloy
  2038. tag: v1.12.0 # or newer known-good in your repo
  2039. </code></pre>
  2040. <ol start="2">
  2041. <li><strong>Use the Loki positions component (not local.file).</strong> Example:</li>
  2042. </ol>
  2043. <pre><code class="language-hcl"># Persist tail offsets here
  2044. loki.positions &quot;pos&quot; {
  2045. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  2046. }
  2047. ​
  2048. discovery.kubernetes &quot;pods&quot; {
  2049. role = &quot;pod&quot;
  2050. }
  2051. ​
  2052. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  2053. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  2054. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  2055. ​
  2056. # only available on newer Alloy for k8s source; if your version complains, remove it
  2057. start_at = &quot;end&quot;
  2058. ​
  2059. positions = loki.positions.pos
  2060. }
  2061. </code></pre>
  2062. <ol start="3">
  2063. <li><strong>Make sure the directory exists and is writable.</strong> You already added:</li>
  2064. </ol>
  2065. <pre><code class="language-yaml">controller:
  2066. volumes:
  2067. extra:
  2068. - name: positions
  2069. emptyDir: {}
  2070. alloy:
  2071. mounts:
  2072. extra:
  2073. - name: positions
  2074. mountPath: /tmp/alloy
  2075. </code></pre>
  2076. <p>That’s perfect—keep it.</p>
  2077. <ol start="4">
  2078. <li><strong>Roll Alloy</strong> after the chart bump and config change.</li>
  2079. </ol>
  2080. <hr>
  2081. <h2>Optional: still seeing 429s/400s?</h2>
  2082. <ul>
  2083. <li>429 means you’re hitting Loki <strong>ingestion rate limits</strong>; either wait it out or temporarily raise <code>limits_config</code> for the <code>core</code> tenant while the backlog drains.</li>
  2084. <li>400 “too far behind” is Loki’s <strong>old-entries window</strong>; if you <em>must</em> backfill, temporarily extend the allowed age (name varies by Loki distro; commonly under <code>limits_config</code>), then revert.</li>
  2085. </ul>
  2086. <hr>
  2087. <h3>TL;DR</h3>
  2088. <ul>
  2089. <li>Remove <code>start_at</code> and the <code>local.file</code> positions reference to unstick v1.10.1 <strong>now</strong>.</li>
  2090. <li>For a durable fix (start-from-end + persisted offsets), <strong>upgrade Alloy</strong> and use <strong><code>loki.positions</code></strong> with <code>filename=&quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;</code>; then reference it in <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code>.</li>
  2091. </ul>
  2092. <p>Got it—two asks:</p>
  2093. <ol>
  2094. <li><strong>Accept “older” logs</strong> (avoid <code>entry too far behind … oldest acceptable timestamp is …</code>)</li>
  2095. <li><strong>Raise ingestion rate/burst</strong> for your tenant(s)</li>
  2096. </ol>
  2097. <p>Below are <strong>safe, Helm-values-only</strong> changes for the Grafana Loki chart you’re already using.</p>
  2098. <hr>
  2099. <h1>Option A — set <strong>global</strong> limits (quick + simple)</h1>
  2100. <p>Add a <code>limits_config</code> block under <code>values.loki</code>:</p>
  2101. <pre><code class="language-yaml"># gitops/apps/loki/release.yaml
  2102. spec:
  2103. values:
  2104. loki:
  2105. auth_enabled: true
  2106. # ... your existing schemaConfig/commonConfig/storage ...
  2107. ​
  2108. # NEW: global limits for all tenants
  2109. limits_config:
  2110. # Accept older logs up to 7 days (tweak as needed)
  2111. reject_old_samples: true
  2112. reject_old_samples_max_age: 168h
  2113. ​
  2114. # Raise write throughput (per-tenant unless overridden)
  2115. ingestion_rate_mb: 16 # was default (~4 MB/s); try 8–32
  2116. ingestion_burst_size_mb: 32 # was default (~8 MB); try 2× rate
  2117. ​
  2118. # (nice-to-haves)
  2119. max_streams_per_user: 0 # 0 = unlimited (or set a sane cap)
  2120. max_global_streams_per_user: 0
  2121. </code></pre>
  2122. <blockquote>
  2123. <p>This immediately:</p>
  2124. <ul>
  2125. <li>Lets Alloy push logs that are up to <strong>7 days old</strong>.</li>
  2126. <li>Increases per-tenant <strong>steady rate</strong> to <strong>16 MB/s</strong> and <strong>burst</strong> to <strong>32 MB</strong>.</li>
  2127. </ul>
  2128. </blockquote>
  2129. <hr>
  2130. <h1>Option B — <strong>per-tenant</strong> overrides (recommended)</h1>
  2131. <p>Keep a modest global default, then give specific tenants (e.g. <code>core</code>, <code>alder</code>) bigger limits, and tune how far behind they can be. This uses Loki’s <strong>runtime config</strong> (hot-reloadable).</p>
  2132. <pre><code class="language-yaml"># gitops/apps/loki/release.yaml
  2133. spec:
  2134. values:
  2135. loki:
  2136. auth_enabled: true
  2137. # ... your existing schemaConfig/commonConfig/storage ...
  2138. ​
  2139. # Baseline defaults (applied to all tenants unless overridden)
  2140. limits_config:
  2141. reject_old_samples: true
  2142. reject_old_samples_max_age: 24h # conservative global default
  2143. ingestion_rate_mb: 4
  2144. ingestion_burst_size_mb: 8
  2145. ​
  2146. # NEW: per-tenant overrides
  2147. runtimeConfig:
  2148. overrides:
  2149. core:
  2150. ingestion_rate_mb: 16
  2151. ingestion_burst_size_mb: 32
  2152. reject_old_samples_max_age: 168h
  2153. alder:
  2154. ingestion_rate_mb: 16
  2155. ingestion_burst_size_mb: 32
  2156. reject_old_samples_max_age: 168h
  2157. </code></pre>
  2158. <blockquote>
  2159. <p>Alloy must send <code>X-Scope-OrgID: core</code> (or <code>alder</code>)—you already do this for <code>core</code>. Do the same in any sender for <code>alder</code>.</p>
  2160. </blockquote>
  2161. <hr>
  2162. <h2>Notes &amp; tips</h2>
  2163. <ul>
  2164. <li><p><strong>Which knob fixes “older logs”?</strong>
  2165. <code>limits_config.reject_old_samples_max_age</code> (increase it). You can leave <code>reject_old_samples: true</code> for safety and simply raise the window.</p>
  2166. </li>
  2167. <li><p><strong>Still seeing 429s?</strong>
  2168. If your write path (gateway → distributor → ingesters) is undersized, also consider bumping <strong><code>write.replicas</code></strong> and CPU/memory on write pods. But raising <code>ingestion_rate_mb</code>/<code>ingestion_burst_size_mb</code> is the first lever.</p>
  2169. </li>
  2170. <li><p><strong>Gateway</strong>
  2171. No change needed; it already forwards the <code>X-Scope-OrgID</code> header. Make sure any new tenant (e.g. <code>alder</code>) sets it on the client side (Alloy, promtail, etc.).</p>
  2172. </li>
  2173. <li><p><strong>Granular control</strong>
  2174. You can add more per-tenant keys under <code>overrides</code> (e.g., <code>max_series_per_user</code>, <code>max_label_names_per_series</code>) if you later hit other limits.</p>
  2175. </li>
  2176. </ul>
  2177. <p>If you want, I can produce a ready-to-commit patch for <strong>Option B</strong> against your current file.</p>
  2178. <p>awesome—let’s do a quick end-to-end smoke for <strong>logs</strong>, plus a note on why your <strong>traces (RED)</strong> panel is likely empty right now.</p>
  2179. <h1>1) Generate log traffic from the <code>netdebug</code> pod</h1>
  2180. <p>From your <em>existing</em> netdebug shell:</p>
  2181. <pre><code class="language-bash"># a) burst some INFO lines
  2182. for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  2183. echo &quot;$(date -Is) level=info app=manual-probe msg=&#39;hello from netdebug&#39; i=$i&quot;
  2184. done
  2185. ​
  2186. # b) sprinkle some ERRORs so the “Error log lines /s” panel has data
  2187. for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  2188. echo &quot;$(date -Is) level=error app=manual-probe msg=&#39;something went wrong&#39; i=$i&quot;
  2189. done
  2190. ​
  2191. # c) keep a steady stream (Ctrl-C to stop)
  2192. while true; do
  2193. r=$((RANDOM%10))
  2194. if [ &quot;$r&quot; -eq 0 ]; then
  2195. echo &quot;$(date -Is) level=error app=manual-probe msg=&#39;periodic failure&#39; trace_id=$(openssl rand -hex 8)&quot;
  2196. else
  2197. echo &quot;$(date -Is) level=info app=manual-probe msg=&#39;heartbeat ok&#39; trace_id=$(openssl rand -hex 8)&quot;
  2198. fi
  2199. sleep 1
  2200. done
  2201. </code></pre>
  2202. <p>Alloy is already tailing stdout for <code>monitoring/netdebug</code>; no extra config needed.</p>
  2203. <h1>2) Verify ingestion directly against Loki (via gateway)</h1>
  2204. <p>Still in the netdebug shell:</p>
  2205. <pre><code class="language-bash">TENANT=core
  2206. Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}&#39;
  2207. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000
  2208. END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  2209. ​
  2210. curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: $TENANT&quot; \
  2211. &#39;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range&#39; \
  2212. --data-urlencode &quot;query=$Q&quot; \
  2213. --data-urlencode &quot;start=$START&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;end=$END&quot; \
  2214. --data-urlencode &quot;limit=20&quot; | jq &#39;.data.result[].values[]&#39;
  2215. </code></pre>
  2216. <p>You should see recent lines (timestamps + your messages).
  2217. Optional: a quick rate check:</p>
  2218. <pre><code class="language-bash">curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: $TENANT&quot; \
  2219. &#39;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range&#39; \
  2220. --data-urlencode &#39;query=sum by (namespace) (rate({namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}[5m]))&#39; \
  2221. --data-urlencode &quot;start=$START&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;end=$END&quot; \
  2222. --data-urlencode &quot;step=30s&quot; | jq &#39;.data.result&#39;
  2223. </code></pre>
  2224. <h1>3) Make sure the <strong>Loki – Operations</strong> dashboard shows data</h1>
  2225. <p>Your queries currently filter on <code>cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;</code>, but Alloy’s <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code> isn’t adding a <code>cluster</code> label. Two quick choices:</p>
  2226. <p><strong>A. Simplest (dashboard-only fix)</strong>
  2227. Edit the dashboard queries to drop the cluster filter:</p>
  2228. <ul>
  2229. <li><code>sum by (namespace) (rate({cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;}[5m]))</code>
  2230. → <code>sum by (namespace) (rate({}[5m]))</code></li>
  2231. <li><code>sum by (namespace) (rate({cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;} |= &quot;error&quot; [5m]))</code>
  2232. → <code>sum by (namespace) (rate({} |= &quot;error&quot; [5m]))</code></li>
  2233. <li>Templating var <code>namespace</code>:
  2234. <code>label_values({cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;}, namespace)</code> → <code>label_values({}, namespace)</code></li>
  2235. </ul>
  2236. <p><strong>B. Keep the cluster filter (pipeline fix)</strong>
  2237. If you want to keep <code>cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;</code>, add that label in Alloy and forward <strong>via a relabel stage</strong> (source → relabel → write). If you want this, say the word and I’ll give you an Alloy-correct snippet wired into your existing config.</p>
  2238. <h1>4) MinIO + Kubernetes dashboards</h1>
  2239. <p>Those use Prometheus/Mimir metrics and should already be live (no manual data generation required). Just open:</p>
  2240. <ul>
  2241. <li>“<strong>MinIO – Health</strong>”: you should see capacity %, nodes online, bucket stats.</li>
  2242. <li>“<strong>Kubernetes – Cluster Overview</strong>”: CPU/mem %, restarts, filesystems, API 5xx.</li>
  2243. </ul>
  2244. <p>If a panel is blank, confirm the datasource on the panel is <code>mimir</code> (you provisioned it), and time range is “Last 15 min”.</p>
  2245. <h1>5) Why the <strong>Service RED (Traces)</strong> dashboard may be empty</h1>
  2246. <p>That dashboard reads <strong>Prometheus spanmetrics</strong> (<code>traces_spanmetrics_*</code>). Your Alloy config only <strong>receives OTLP</strong> and forwards to <strong>Tempo</strong>, but you don’t have a <strong>metrics generator</strong> in place.</p>
  2247. <p>Two ways to populate those metrics:</p>
  2248. <p><strong>Option 1 — Tempo metrics-generator (recommended)</strong>
  2249. Configure Tempo with metrics-generator and remote_write to Mimir. Example (values snippet):</p>
  2250. <pre><code class="language-yaml">tempo:
  2251. metricsGenerator:
  2252. enabled: true
  2253. remoteWrite:
  2254. - url: http://mimir-nginx.mimir.svc.cluster.local/api/v1/push
  2255. sendExemplars: true
  2256. headers:
  2257. X-Scope-OrgID: corelocal
  2258. </code></pre>
  2259. <p><strong>Option 2 — Generate spanmetrics in Alloy</strong>
  2260. Add an <code>otelcol.processor.spanmetrics</code> pipeline in Alloy, then export those metrics to Mimir (either via Prom remote_write exporter or OTLP -&gt; Prometheus remote-write bridge). I can craft an exact Alloy stanza if you prefer this route.</p>
  2261. <h1>6) (Optional) Push logs as a separate tenant (e.g., <code>alder</code>)</h1>
  2262. <p>If you want to test per-tenant limits/overrides:</p>
  2263. <pre><code class="language-bash">TS=$(date +%s)000000000
  2264. BODY=&#39;{&quot;streams&quot;:[{&quot;stream&quot;:{&quot;app&quot;:&quot;tenant-test&quot;,&quot;namespace&quot;:&quot;monitoring&quot;,&quot;pod&quot;:&quot;netdebug&quot;,&quot;cluster&quot;:&quot;corelocal&quot;},&quot;values&quot;:[[&quot;&#39;&quot;$TS&quot;&#39;&quot;,&quot;hello from alder tenant&quot;]]}]}&#39;
  2265. curl -sS -H &#39;Content-Type: application/json&#39; -H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: alder&#39; \
  2266. -X POST --data &quot;$BODY&quot; \
  2267. http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push
  2268. </code></pre>
  2269. <p>Then query with <code>-H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: alder&#39;</code>.</p>
