  2328. <h1>C) Make the <strong>Loki – Operations</strong> dashboard show data</h1>
  2329. <p>Your dashboard queries use <code>cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;</code>, but your Alloy pipeline doesn’t add that label. Two clean ways to fix:</p>
  2330. <h3>Option 1 (quickest): remove the cluster filter in the dashboard</h3>
  2331. <ul>
  2332. <li><p><code>sum by (namespace) (rate({cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;}[5m]))</code> → <code>sum by (namespace) (rate({}[5m]))</code></p>
  2333. </li>
  2334. <li><p><code>sum by (namespace) (rate({cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;} |= &quot;error&quot; [5m]))</code> → <code>sum by (namespace) (rate({} |= &quot;error&quot; [5m]))</code></p>
  2335. </li>
  2336. <li><p>Templating var:</p>
  2337. <ul>
  2338. <li><code>label_values({cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;}, namespace)</code> → <code>label_values({}, namespace)</code></li>
  2339. </ul>
  2340. </li>
  2341. </ul>
  2342. <h3>Option 2 (preferred for multi-cluster hygiene): stamp the cluster label in Alloy</h3>
  2343. <p>Add a tiny process stage and forward logs through it:</p>
  2344. <pre><code class="language-alloy">discovery.kubernetes &quot;pods&quot; {
  2345. role = &quot;pod&quot;
  2346. }
  2347. ​
  2348. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  2349. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  2350. forward_to = [loki.process.add_cluster_label.receiver]
  2351. }
  2352. ​
  2353. loki.process &quot;add_cluster_label&quot; {
  2354. stage.static_labels {
  2355. values = { cluster = &quot;corelocal&quot; }
  2356. }
  2357. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  2358. }
  2359. ​
  2360. loki.write &quot;loki&quot; {
  2361. endpoint {
  2362. url = &quot;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push&quot;
  2363. tenant_id = &quot;core&quot;
  2364. }
  2365. }
  2366. </code></pre>
  2367. <blockquote>
  2368. <p>This preserves your dashboards as-is and helps later if you add more clusters.</p>
  2369. </blockquote>
  2370. <hr>
  2371. <h1>D) Retest dashboards</h1>
  2372. <ul>
  2373. <li><strong>MinIO – Health</strong> / <strong>Kubernetes – Cluster Overview</strong> use Prometheus/Mimir — they should already show data. Just set a recent time window (e.g., <strong>Last 15 min</strong>).</li>
  2374. <li><strong>Loki – Operations</strong>: after (C), you’ll see spikes for the bursts and steady lines/sec from the loop. The “Error log lines /s” panel should tick up when the loop logs <code>level=error</code>.</li>
  2375. </ul>
  2376. <hr>
  2377. <h1>E) Why <strong>Service RED (Requests, Errors, Duration)</strong> may be empty (and how to fix)</h1>
  2378. <p>That dashboard reads <strong><code>traces_spanmetrics_*</code></strong>. You don’t currently generate those. Pick one:</p>
  2379. <h3>Tempo metrics-generator (simple + recommended)</h3>
  2380. <p>Enable in Tempo and remote-write to Mimir:</p>
  2381. <pre><code class="language-yaml">tempo:
  2382. metricsGenerator:
  2383. enabled: true
  2384. remoteWrite:
  2385. - url: http://mimir-nginx.mimir.svc.cluster.local/api/v1/push
  2386. sendExemplars: true
  2387. headers:
  2388. X-Scope-OrgID: corelocal
  2389. </code></pre>
  2390. <p><em>(Exact stanza depends on your Tempo Helm values; I can tailor it if you drop your Tempo release YAML.)</em></p>
  2391. <h3>OR: Spanmetrics in Alloy</h3>
  2392. <p>Add an <code>otelcol.processor.spanmetrics</code> in Alloy’s OTEL pipeline and export those metrics to Mimir. If you prefer Alloy to own this, say so and I’ll hand you a drop-in snippet for your current <code>otelcol.receiver.otlp &quot;ingest&quot;</code> graph.</p>
  2393. <hr>
  2394. <h1>F) (Optional) Test another tenant (e.g., <code>alder</code>)</h1>
  2395. <p>Useful if you want to exercise per-tenant overrides/limits:</p>
  2396. <pre><code class="language-bash">TS=$(date +%s)000000000
  2397. BODY=&#39;{&quot;streams&quot;:[{&quot;stream&quot;:{&quot;app&quot;:&quot;tenant-test&quot;,&quot;namespace&quot;:&quot;monitoring&quot;,&quot;pod&quot;:&quot;netdebug&quot;,&quot;cluster&quot;:&quot;corelocal&quot;},&quot;values&quot;:[[&quot;&#39;&quot;$TS&quot;&#39;&quot;,&quot;hello from alder&quot;]]}]}&#39;
  2398. ​
  2399. curl -sS -H &#39;Content-Type: application/json&#39; -H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: alder&#39; \
  2400. -X POST --data &quot;$BODY&quot; \
  2401. http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push
  2402. </code></pre>
  2403. <p>Then query with <code>-H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: alder&#39;</code>.</p>
  2404. <hr>
  2405. <p>Want me to:</p>
  2406. <ul>
  2407. <li>patch Alloy to add the <code>cluster</code> label,</li>
  2408. <li>or patch the dashboard JSON to drop the cluster filter,</li>
  2409. <li>and provide the exact <strong>Tempo</strong> metrics-generator values block you can commit?</li>
  2410. </ul>
  2411. <p>Tell me which route you want; I’ll give you the ready-to-paste YAML.</p>
  2412. <p>Good clues in those logs:</p>
  2413. <ul>
  2414. <li><p>Alloy is <strong>tailing pods</strong> just fine (<code>opened log stream …</code>).</p>
  2415. </li>
  2416. <li><p>But every push to Loki via the <strong>gateway</strong> returns <strong>502 Bad Gateway</strong>:</p>
  2417. <pre><code>error sending batch ... host=loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local status=502
  2418. </code></pre>
  2419. </li>
  2420. </ul>
  2421. <p>That means ingestion is dying at the gateway, not at Alloy or the Loki write path.</p>
  2422. <h2>Root cause (very likely)</h2>
  2423. <p>Your Helm values override <strong><code>gateway.nginxConfig</code></strong> with only a <code>resolver</code> line:</p>
  2424. <pre><code class="language-yaml">gateway:
  2425. enabled: true
  2426. nginxConfig:
  2427. resolver: &quot;10.152.183.10&quot;
  2428. </code></pre>
  2429. <p>In the Loki Helm chart, <strong>setting <code>gateway.nginxConfig</code> replaces the entire nginx.conf</strong>. Because the default upstream <code>location</code> blocks are gone, NGINX has no route for <code>/loki/api/v1/push</code> (or query endpoints), so it returns <strong>502</strong>. That’s why Alloy can tail but can’t push.</p>
  2430. <h3>Fix (preferred): remove the override and use the chart’s default gateway config</h3>
  2431. <p>Minimal change to your <code>gitops/apps/loki/release.yaml</code>:</p>
  2432. <pre><code class="language-diff"> spec:
  2433. values:
  2434. gateway:
  2435. enabled: true
  2436. - nginxConfig:
  2437. - resolver: &quot;10.152.183.10&quot;
  2438. podAntiAffinity: &quot;&quot;
  2439. </code></pre>
  2440. <p>Apply that and let Flux reconcile. The chart’s stock gateway config correctly proxies:</p>
  2441. <ul>
  2442. <li><strong>push</strong> → distributor/write path</li>
  2443. <li><strong>query</strong> → query-frontend/read path</li>
  2444. <li><strong>ruler</strong>/API → appropriate backends</li>
  2445. </ul>
  2446. <p><em>(If you must keep a custom NGINX config, you need to supply the <strong>entire</strong> working config, including the upstreams and <code>location</code> blocks for <code>/loki/api</code>, <code>/api/prom</code>, ruler, etc. Happy to provide a full, known-good nginx.conf if you want that route.)</em></p>
  2447. <hr>
  2448. <h2>Quick sanity checks after the fix</h2>
  2449. <p>From the <code>netdebug</code> shell:</p>
  2450. <ol>
  2451. <li><strong>Push probe</strong> (bypass Alloy)</li>
  2452. </ol>
  2453. <pre><code class="language-bash">TS=$(date +%s)000000000
  2454. cat &lt;&lt;&#39;JSON&#39; &gt; /tmp/push.json
  2455. {&quot;streams&quot;:[{&quot;stream&quot;:{&quot;namespace&quot;:&quot;monitoring&quot;,&quot;pod&quot;:&quot;netdebug&quot;,&quot;app&quot;:&quot;manual-probe&quot;},&quot;values&quot;:[[&quot;TS_REPLACE&quot;,&quot;hello from gateway&quot;]]}]}
  2456. JSON
  2457. sed -i &quot;s/TS_REPLACE/$TS/&quot; /tmp/push.json
  2458. ​
  2459. curl -sS -H &#39;Content-Type: application/json&#39; -H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: core&#39; \
  2460. -X POST --data @/tmp/push.json \
  2461. http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push -i
  2462. </code></pre>
  2463. <p>Expect <code>HTTP/1.1 204 No Content</code>.</p>
  2464. <ol start="2">
  2465. <li><strong>Query probe</strong></li>
  2466. </ol>
  2467. <pre><code class="language-bash">TENANT=core
  2468. Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}&#39;
  2469. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000
  2470. END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  2471. ​
  2472. curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: $TENANT&quot; \
  2473. &#39;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range&#39; \
  2474. --data-urlencode &quot;query=$Q&quot; \
  2475. --data-urlencode &quot;start=$START&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;end=$END&quot; \
  2476. --data-urlencode &quot;limit=20&quot; | jq &#39;.data.result&#39;
  2477. </code></pre>
  2478. <p>You should now see results (not <code>[]</code>).</p>
  2479. <blockquote>
  2480. <p>If you still get a 502, try <strong>bypassing the gateway</strong> to confirm Loki core works:</p>
  2481. <pre><code>curl -sS -H &#39;Content-Type: application/json&#39; -H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: core&#39; \
  2482. -X POST --data @/tmp/push.json \
  2483. http://loki-write.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push -i
  2484. </code></pre>
  2485. <p>If that succeeds, it’s definitely an NGINX/gateway config issue.</p>
  2486. </blockquote>
  2487. <hr>
  2488. <h2>Bonus: make Alloy tail sanely + (optional) add a cluster label</h2>
  2489. <p>Right now you see <code>&quot;start time&quot;=1970-01-01</code> because the Kubernetes source doesn’t support <code>start_at</code>, and you didn’t wire positions. Use the <strong>correct positions component</strong> (it’s <code>loki.positions</code>, not <code>local.file</code>) so Alloy remembers offsets and won’t re-read from the beginning on restarts:</p>
  2490. <pre><code class="language-alloy">discovery.kubernetes &quot;pods&quot; { role = &quot;pod&quot; }
  2491. ​
  2492. loki.positions &quot;pos&quot; {
  2493. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  2494. }
  2495. ​
  2496. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  2497. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  2498. positions = loki.positions.pos
  2499. forward_to = [loki.process.add_cluster_label.receiver] # optional stage below
  2500. }
  2501. ​
  2502. loki.process &quot;add_cluster_label&quot; {
  2503. stage.static_labels { values = { cluster = &quot;corelocal&quot; } }
  2504. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  2505. }
  2506. ​
  2507. loki.write &quot;loki&quot; {
  2508. endpoint {
  2509. url = &quot;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push&quot;
  2510. tenant_id = &quot;core&quot;
  2511. }
  2512. }
  2513. </code></pre>
  2514. <blockquote>
  2515. <p>Mount <code>/tmp/alloy</code> as you already do. This fixes offset tracking, and adds <code>cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;</code> so your existing dashboard filters work without edits.</p>
  2516. </blockquote>
  2517. <hr>
  2518. <h2>Optional: raise ingestion rate/burst (per-tenant)</h2>
  2519. <p>If you plan to hammer Loki (e.g., alder tenant load), add/adjust <strong>overrides</strong>. With the distributed chart, you can set per-tenant limits via the overrides config (values keys vary by chart version), e.g.:</p>
  2520. <pre><code class="language-yaml">loki:
  2521. limits_config:
  2522. ingestion_rate_mb: 32
  2523. ingestion_burst_size_mb: 64
  2524. max_streams_per_user: 5000
  2525. ruler:
  2526. # …
  2527. # Or via overrides_config per tenant (alder/core) if you keep auth_enabled: true
  2528. </code></pre>
  2529. <p>Tell me your chart version (or paste <code>helm show values grafana/loki | head -n 50</code>) and I’ll give you the exact stanza for <strong>rate/burst</strong> and <strong>per-tenant</strong> (e.g., <code>alder</code>).</p>
  2530. <hr>
  2531. <h3>TL;DR</h3>
  2532. <ul>
  2533. <li>Your <strong>502</strong> is because <code>gateway.nginxConfig</code> replaced the default and removed the routes. <strong>Delete that block</strong> (or supply a full nginx.conf).</li>
  2534. <li>Wire <strong><code>loki.positions</code></strong> in Alloy (not <code>local.file</code>) so it doesn’t re-read from epoch.</li>
  2535. <li>(Optional) add a <strong>cluster label</strong> in Alloy to match your dashboards.</li>
  2536. <li>Then rerun the netdebug push/query probes; your Grafana panels should light up.</li>
  2537. </ul>
  2538. <p>You’re <em>very</em> close. Two things are happening:</p>
  2539. <ol>
  2540. <li><strong>Loki gateway flapped</strong> during rollout → Alloy saw <code>connection refused</code>.</li>
  2541. <li>Alloy is <strong>replaying old timestamps</strong>, and Loki is <strong>rejecting them as too old</strong>:</li>
  2542. </ol>
  2543. <pre><code>HTTP 400 … entry too far behind … oldest acceptable timestamp is: 2025-09-12T14:09:30Z
  2544. </code></pre>
  2545. <p>(while Alloy logs show <code>&quot;start time&quot;=1970-01-01</code> → classic “no positions file wired” symptom)</p>
  2546. <p>Here’s how to fix it cleanly.</p>
  2547. <hr>
  2548. <h2>1) Make Alloy tail from <em>now</em> and remember offsets</h2>
  2549. <p>Update your Alloy <code>configMap</code> content to use <strong><code>loki.positions</code></strong> and point <code>pod_logs.positions</code> at it (don’t use <code>start_at</code>, your Alloy version doesn’t support that):</p>
  2550. <pre><code class="language-hcl">discovery.kubernetes &quot;pods&quot; { role = &quot;pod&quot; }
  2551. ​
  2552. loki.positions &quot;pos&quot; {
  2553. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  2554. }
  2555. ​
  2556. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  2557. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  2558. positions = loki.positions.pos
  2559. forward_to = [loki.process.labels.receiver]
  2560. }
  2561. ​
  2562. # (optional) add a cluster label your dashboards expect
  2563. loki.process &quot;labels&quot; {
  2564. stage.static_labels { values = { cluster = &quot;corelocal&quot; } }
  2565. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  2566. }
  2567. ​
  2568. loki.write &quot;loki&quot; {
  2569. endpoint {
  2570. url = &quot;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push&quot;
  2571. tenant_id = &quot;core&quot;
  2572. }
  2573. }
  2574. </code></pre>
  2575. <p>You already mount <code>/tmp/alloy</code> via an <code>emptyDir</code>—perfect. After applying, <strong>restart the Alloy DaemonSet</strong> once the gateway is stable. New entries will be tailed with fresh timestamps and won’t be rejected.</p>
  2576. <blockquote>
  2577. <p>Why you saw “entry too far behind”: with no valid positions, the k8s source re-opened very old log cursors. Loki’s default ingest window only accepts <em>recent</em> events (roughly last ~1h by default), so it 400’d the backlog.</p>
  2578. </blockquote>
  2579. <hr>
  2580. <h2>2) Keep the gateway up during rollouts</h2>
  2581. <p>Your logs show several minutes of:</p>
  2582. <pre><code>… dial tcp … connect: connection refused
  2583. </code></pre>
  2584. <p>That’s just the gateway being restarted with <strong>1 replica</strong>. Give it 2 replicas so there’s no ingest blackout:</p>
  2585. <pre><code class="language-yaml"># gitops/apps/loki/release.yaml
  2586. values:
  2587. gateway:
  2588. enabled: true
  2589. replicas: 2
  2590. podAntiAffinity: &quot;&quot;
  2591. </code></pre>
  2592. <p><em>(You can also add a PDB later, but 2 replicas is the quick win.)</em></p>
  2593. <hr>
  2594. <h2>3) Your Loki limits look fine for rate/burst</h2>
  2595. <p>You’ve set:</p>
  2596. <pre><code class="language-yaml">loki:
  2597. limits_config:
  2598. ingestion_rate_mb: 16
  2599. ingestion_burst_size_mb: 32
  2600. max_streams_per_user: 0
  2601. max_global_streams_per_user: 0
  2602. </code></pre>
  2603. <p>That’s good for testing and more than enough for Alloy + netdebug. No change needed here.</p>
  2604. <hr>
  2605. <h2>4) Quick verifications (run after applying the two changes)</h2>
  2606. <p><strong>A. Push a line directly to Loki (bypasses Alloy), expect 204:</strong></p>
  2607. <pre><code class="language-bash">TS=$(date +%s)000000000
  2608. cat &gt;/tmp/push.json &lt;&lt;&#39;JSON&#39;
  2609. {&quot;streams&quot;:[{&quot;stream&quot;:{&quot;namespace&quot;:&quot;monitoring&quot;,&quot;pod&quot;:&quot;netdebug&quot;,&quot;app&quot;:&quot;manual-probe&quot;},&quot;values&quot;:[[&quot;TS_REPLACE&quot;,&quot;hello from gateway&quot;]]}]}
  2610. JSON
  2611. sed -i &quot;s/TS_REPLACE/$TS/&quot; /tmp/push.json
  2612. ​
  2613. curl -i -H &#39;Content-Type: application/json&#39; -H &#39;X-Scope-OrgID: core&#39; \
  2614. -X POST --data @/tmp/push.json \
  2615. http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push
  2616. </code></pre>
  2617. <p><strong>B. Query the last 10 minutes, expect non-empty results:</strong></p>
  2618. <pre><code class="language-bash">TENANT=core
  2619. Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}&#39;
  2620. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000
  2621. END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  2622. ​
  2623. curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: $TENANT&quot; \
  2624. &#39;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range&#39; \
  2625. --data-urlencode &quot;query=$Q&quot; \
  2626. --data-urlencode &quot;start=$START&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;end=$END&quot; \
  2627. --data-urlencode &quot;limit=20&quot; | jq &#39;.data.result&#39;
  2628. </code></pre>
  2629. <p><strong>C. Check Alloy logs stop saying <code>&quot;start time&quot;=1970-01-01</code></strong> and stop emitting “entry too far behind”.</p>
  2630. <hr>
  2631. <h2>5) If you <em>do</em> need to ingest older backfill later</h2>
  2632. <p>Once everything’s flowing, and only if you truly need historical ingestion, you can relax out-of-order/oldness limits temporarily (tenant-level overrides). But for live cluster logs, the better practice is what we’re doing: <strong>start tailing from now</strong> and let the old stuff go.</p>
  2633. <hr>
  2634. <h3>TL;DR</h3>
  2635. <ul>
  2636. <li>Wire <strong><code>loki.positions</code></strong> in Alloy and remove <code>start_at</code>.</li>
  2637. <li><strong>Scale gateway to 2 replicas</strong> to avoid ingest outages.</li>
  2638. <li>Retest with the curl probes; your Grafana Loki panels should light up.</li>
  2639. </ul>
  2640. <p>Your Alloy binary is older than the config I gave you. This build <strong>doesn’t have <code>loki.positions</code> or <code>loki.process</code> components</strong>, which is why you’re getting:</p>
  2641. <pre><code>cannot find the definition of component name &quot;loki.positions&quot;
  2642. … &quot;loki.process.labels.receiver&quot; does not exist …
  2643. </code></pre>
  2644. <p>Those components (and the <code>start_at</code> attribute on <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code>) landed in newer Alloy releases. Fix is to <strong>upgrade the Alloy chart/image</strong>, then apply the newer config.</p>
  2645. <h2>What to change</h2>
  2646. <h3>1) Bump the Alloy chart/image</h3>
  2647. <p>In your <code>gitops/apps/alloy/release.yaml</code>:</p>
  2648. <pre><code class="language-yaml">spec:
  2649. chart:
  2650. spec:
  2651. chart: alloy
  2652. # pick a recent version that ships Alloy &gt;= v1.5.x
  2653. version: 1.9.0 # (example; any recent 1.8+/1.9+ works)
  2654. values:
  2655. alloy:
  2656. image:
  2657. repository: grafana/alloy
  2658. tag: v1.5.0 # or newer (v1.6.x works too)
  2659. </code></pre>
  2660. <p>(If your chart doesn’t expose <code>alloy.image.tag</code>, use <code>controller.image</code> or the chart’s documented image override—names vary a bit across minor chart releases.)</p>
  2661. <p>You already mount a writeable positions directory; keep that:</p>
  2662. <ul>
  2663. <li><code>volumes.extra: { name: positions, emptyDir: {} }</code></li>
  2664. <li><code>mounts.extra: { name: positions, mountPath: /tmp/alloy }</code></li>
  2665. </ul>
  2666. <h3>2) Use the positions-aware config</h3>
  2667. <p>Replace the Alloy <code>configMap.content</code> with this (works on Alloy ≥ v1.5):</p>
  2668. <pre><code class="language-hcl">logging {
  2669. level = &quot;info&quot;
  2670. format = &quot;logfmt&quot;
  2671. }
  2672. ​
  2673. discovery.kubernetes &quot;pods&quot; {
  2674. role = &quot;pod&quot;
  2675. }
  2676. ​
  2677. loki.positions &quot;pos&quot; {
  2678. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  2679. }
  2680. ​
  2681. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  2682. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  2683. positions = loki.positions.pos
  2684. forward_to = [loki.process.labels.receiver]
  2685. }
  2686. ​
  2687. loki.process &quot;labels&quot; {
  2688. stage.static_labels { values = { cluster = &quot;corelocal&quot; } }
  2689. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  2690. }
  2691. ​
  2692. loki.write &quot;loki&quot; {
  2693. endpoint {
  2694. url = &quot;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push&quot;
  2695. tenant_id = &quot;core&quot;
  2696. }
  2697. }
  2698. ​
  2699. otelcol.receiver.otlp &quot;ingest&quot; {
  2700. grpc { endpoint = &quot;0.0.0.0:4317&quot; }
  2701. http { endpoint = &quot;0.0.0.0:4318&quot; }
  2702. output { traces = [otelcol.exporter.otlp.tempo.input] }
  2703. }
  2704. ​
  2705. otelcol.exporter.otlp &quot;tempo&quot; {
  2706. client {
  2707. endpoint = &quot;http://tempo.tempo.svc.cluster.local:4317&quot;
  2708. tls { insecure = true }
  2709. }
  2710. }
  2711. </code></pre>
  2712. <blockquote>
  2713. <p>Note: With these versions, <strong>you do not need <code>start_at</code></strong>; using <code>loki.positions</code> ensures Alloy tails from “now” after the first start and persists offsets.</p>
  2714. </blockquote>
  2715. <h3>3) Keep the Loki gateway at 2 replicas</h3>
  2716. <p>You already scaled the gateway to <code>replicas: 2</code>—great. That prevents the “connection refused” blips during rollouts.</p>
  2717. <h2>After you commit</h2>
  2718. <ol>
  2719. <li>Let Flux roll out the Alloy upgrade (wait for pods to be Running/Ready).</li>
  2720. <li><strong>Bounce Alloy once</strong> after the new config is live (to seed the positions file).</li>
  2721. <li>Re-run your <code>netdebug</code> log spam and the <code>curl …/query_range</code> checks. You should see results in Grafana and via curl.</li>
  2722. </ol>
  2723. <p>If you prefer not to upgrade Alloy, the only alternative is to fall back to the older pattern (no <code>loki.process</code>, and using the legacy, unsupported <code>local.file</code> won’t work for positions). Upgrading is the clean, supported path.</p>
  2724. <hr>
  2725. <p>Good catch—Flux is telling you exactly why Alloy isn’t changing:</p>
  2726. <ul>
  2727. <li><code>reconciliation stalled … no &#39;alloy&#39; chart with version matching &#39;1.9.0&#39; found</code></li>
  2728. </ul>
  2729. <p>So the new config never rolled out; you’re still on the <strong>old chart/app</strong> that doesn’t support <code>loki.positions</code> / <code>loki.process</code>.</p>
  2730. <p>Here’s the fastest path to green:</p>
  2731. <h2>1) Stop pinning to a non-existent chart version</h2>
  2732. <p>In <code>gitops/apps/alloy/release.yaml</code>, either:</p>
  2733. <ul>
  2734. <li><strong>Option A (safe):</strong> keep your known-good chart <code>1.2.1</code> and only bump the <strong>image tag</strong> (the chart and the app versions are independent), or</li>
  2735. <li><strong>Option B:</strong> set a <strong>real</strong> chart version that exists in the Grafana repo.</li>
  2736. </ul>
  2737. <p>Since we don’t have a verified list here, go with <strong>Option A</strong>:</p>
  2738. <pre><code class="language-yaml">spec:
  2739. chart:
  2740. spec:
  2741. chart: alloy
  2742. version: 1.2.1 # keep this (it exists)
  2743. sourceRef:
  2744. kind: HelmRepository
  2745. name: grafana
  2746. namespace: flux-system
  2747. values:
  2748. alloy:
  2749. image:
  2750. repository: grafana/alloy
  2751. tag: v1.6.0 # any v1.5+ has loki.positions/loki.process
  2752. pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  2753. </code></pre>
  2754. <p>(If your chart uses a different path for the image override, adapt accordingly—some revisions use <code>controller.image</code> or <code>image.tag</code>. The idea is: <strong>chart can stay</strong>, <strong>app image must be ≥ v1.5</strong>.)</p>
  2755. <h2>2) Use a config that matches the newer Alloy</h2>
  2756. <p>Keep the positions file you already mounted and use this Alloy config (no <code>start_at</code> needed):</p>
  2757. <pre><code class="language-hcl">logging {
  2758. level = &quot;info&quot;
  2759. format = &quot;logfmt&quot;
  2760. }
  2761. ​
  2762. discovery.kubernetes &quot;pods&quot; { role = &quot;pod&quot; }
  2763. ​
  2764. loki.positions &quot;pos&quot; {
  2765. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  2766. }
  2767. ​
  2768. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  2769. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  2770. positions = loki.positions.pos
  2771. forward_to = [loki.process.labels.receiver]
  2772. }
  2773. ​
  2774. loki.process &quot;labels&quot; {
  2775. stage.static_labels { values = { cluster = &quot;corelocal&quot; } }
  2776. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  2777. }
  2778. ​
  2779. loki.write &quot;loki&quot; {
  2780. endpoint {
  2781. url = &quot;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push&quot;
  2782. tenant_id = &quot;core&quot;
  2783. }
  2784. }
  2785. ​
  2786. otelcol.receiver.otlp &quot;ingest&quot; {
  2787. grpc { endpoint = &quot;0.0.0.0:4317&quot; }
  2788. http { endpoint = &quot;0.0.0.0:4318&quot; }
  2789. output { traces = [otelcol.exporter.otlp.tempo.input] }
  2790. }
  2791. ​
  2792. otelcol.exporter.otlp &quot;tempo&quot; {
  2793. client {
  2794. endpoint = &quot;http://tempo.tempo.svc.cluster.local:4317&quot;
  2795. tls { insecure = true }
  2796. }
  2797. }
  2798. </code></pre>
  2799. <h2>3) Commit and watch Flux</h2>
  2800. <p>You should see Flux switch from the “stalled invalid chart reference” error to a normal HelmChart fetch, then a rollout of <code>monitoring/alloy-*</code>.</p>
  2801. <p>Quick checks:</p>
  2802. <pre><code class="language-bash"># Helm release status
  2803. kubectl -n monitoring get hr alloy -o wide
  2804. kubectl -n monitoring describe hr alloy
  2805. ​
  2806. # Alloy pods and logs
  2807. kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy
  2808. kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/alloy --tail=200
  2809. </code></pre>
  2810. <h2>4) Sanity checks on Loki side (you already addressed most)</h2>
  2811. <ul>
  2812. <li><p>You scaled <strong>gateway to 2 replicas</strong> (great) to avoid 502/connection-refused during rollouts.</p>
  2813. </li>
  2814. <li><p>You set:</p>
  2815. <pre><code class="language-yaml">limits_config:
  2816. reject_old_samples: true
  2817. reject_old_samples_max_age: 168h
  2818. ingestion_rate_mb: 16
  2819. ingestion_burst_size_mb: 32
  2820. max_streams_per_user: 0
  2821. max_global_streams_per_user: 0
  2822. </code></pre>
  2823. <p>That eliminates the earlier “entry too far behind” and unlocks rates/bursts.</p>
  2824. </li>
  2825. </ul>
  2826. <h2>5) Re-test the flow</h2>
  2827. <p>From your <code>netdebug</code> pod:</p>
  2828. <pre><code class="language-bash">TENANT=core
  2829. Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}&#39;
  2830. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000
  2831. END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  2832. ​
  2833. curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: $TENANT&quot; \
  2834. &#39;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range&#39; \
  2835. --data-urlencode &quot;query=$Q&quot; \
  2836. --data-urlencode &quot;start=$START&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;end=$END&quot; \
  2837. --data-urlencode &quot;limit=20&quot; | jq &#39;.data.result[].values[]&#39;
  2838. </code></pre>
  2839. <p>…and peek at Grafana’s Loki datasource → Explore to confirm.</p>
  2840. <hr>
  2841. <h3>Why this fixes your Flux loop</h3>
  2842. <p>Flux shows repeated lines like:</p>
  2843. <pre><code>HelmChart/monitoring-alloy.flux-system - artifact up-to-date with remote revision: &#39;1.2.1&#39;
  2844. …
  2845. reconciliation stalled invalid chart reference … &#39;1.9.0&#39; not found
  2846. </code></pre>
  2847. <p>That means the HelmRepository is healthy, but <strong>the version you pinned doesn’t exist</strong>, so Flux can’t fetch the chart → no release → your new config/image never lands. Pinning to a valid chart + bumping the <strong>image tag</strong> to a supported Alloy version unblocks reconciliation and gives you the new Loki components support.</p>
  2848. <p>Progress! Loki itself is healthy (canary pushes get 204s; queries 200s), so the gap is <strong>Alloy failing to load your config</strong>. The errors:</p>
  2849. <pre><code>cannot find the definition of component name &quot;loki.positions&quot;
  2850. component &quot;loki.process.labels&quot; does not exist
  2851. </code></pre>
  2852. <p>mean the <strong>running Alloy binary doesn’t include those components</strong> (it’s too old), even though you set <code>tag: v1.6.0</code> in values. Most likely the image override isn’t wired to the chart key your Helm release actually uses, so the pod is still running the chart’s default (older) image.</p>
  2853. <h3>Fix it in 3 steps</h3>
  2854. <ol>
  2855. <li><strong>Confirm what image is really running</strong></li>
  2856. </ol>
  2857. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy -o jsonpath=&#39;{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{&quot; &quot;}{.spec.containers[0].image}{&quot;\n&quot;}{end}&#39;
  2858. </code></pre>
  2859. <p>If it’s not <code>grafana/alloy:v1.5+</code>, your override didn’t apply.</p>
  2860. <ol start="2">
  2861. <li><strong>Set the right Helm values so the image actually bumps</strong>
  2862. Different chart versions use different keys. With your chart <code>version: 1.2.1</code>, cover the common ones (belt-and-suspenders):</li>
  2863. </ol>
  2864. <pre><code class="language-yaml">values:
  2865. # some chart versions use this:
  2866. image:
  2867. repository: grafana/alloy
  2868. tag: v1.6.1
  2869. pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  2870. ​
  2871. # others use this nested key:
  2872. alloy:
  2873. image:
  2874. repository: grafana/alloy
  2875. tag: v1.6.1
  2876. pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  2877. ​
  2878. # and a few wire it under controller.*:
  2879. controller:
  2880. image:
  2881. repository: grafana/alloy
  2882. tag: v1.6.1
  2883. pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  2884. </code></pre>
  2885. <p>Commit, let Flux reconcile, and re-check the running image (step 1). Don’t change the chart version right now—just make sure the <strong>app image</strong> is ≥ v1.5.</p>
  2886. <ol start="3">
  2887. <li><strong>Keep the Alloy config you have now</strong>
  2888. Once the pod is actually on v1.5+ the config you posted will parse:</li>
  2889. </ol>
  2890. <pre><code class="language-river">discovery.kubernetes &quot;pods&quot; { role = &quot;pod&quot; }
  2891. ​
  2892. loki.positions &quot;pos&quot; {
  2893. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  2894. }
  2895. ​
  2896. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  2897. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  2898. positions = loki.positions.pos
  2899. forward_to = [loki.process.labels.receiver]
  2900. }
  2901. ​
  2902. loki.process &quot;labels&quot; {
  2903. stage.static_labels { values = { cluster = &quot;corelocal&quot; } }
  2904. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  2905. }
  2906. ​
  2907. loki.write &quot;loki&quot; {
  2908. endpoint {
  2909. url = &quot;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push&quot;
  2910. tenant_id = &quot;core&quot;
  2911. }
  2912. }
  2913. </code></pre>
  2914. <h3>Quick health checks after rollout</h3>
  2915. <ul>
  2916. <li>Alloy should go <strong>Running</strong> with no “cannot find component” errors:</li>
  2917. </ul>
  2918. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200
  2919. </code></pre>
  2920. <ul>
  2921. <li>You should see batches <strong>successfully pushed</strong> from Alloy, and queries return your <code>netdebug</code> lines:</li>
  2922. </ul>
  2923. <pre><code class="language-bash">TENANT=core
  2924. Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}&#39;
  2925. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000; END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  2926. curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: $TENANT&quot; \
  2927. &#39;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range&#39; \
  2928. --data-urlencode &quot;query=$Q&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;start=$START&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;end=$END&quot; \
  2929. --data-urlencode &quot;limit=20&quot; | jq &#39;.data.result[].values[]&#39;
  2930. </code></pre>
  2931. <h3>Why this is the blocker</h3>
  2932. <ul>
  2933. <li><code>local.file</code> is a <strong>file reader</strong>, not a positions tracker—so it failed earlier (“no such file”).</li>
  2934. <li><code>loki.positions</code> / <code>loki.process</code> are <strong>newer Alloy components</strong>. Your pod is still on an older binary that doesn’t have them, hence the “cannot find component” parse errors. Once the image is really v1.5+ the config loads and shipping starts.</li>
  2935. </ul>
  2936. <p>If you want, paste the output of the “what image is running” command and I’ll tell you exactly which key your chart expects for the image override.</p>
  2937. <p>Nice — Alloy is now actually running <strong>v1.10.1</strong>:</p>
  2938. <pre><code>alloy-s8jkj docker.io/grafana/alloy:v1.10.1
  2939. </code></pre>
  2940. <p>At that version, the Loki components you’re using <strong>exist</strong>, but they’re <strong>gated by stability levels</strong>. If Alloy is started with the default (<code>public</code> only), components like <code>loki.positions</code>, <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code>, and <code>loki.process</code> won’t be registered and you’ll see exactly the “cannot find the definition of component name&quot; errors you hit.</p>
  2941. <h2>What to do</h2>
  2942. <p>Add the stability flag so beta components are enabled:</p>
  2943. <pre><code class="language-yaml"># gitops/apps/alloy/release.yaml
  2944. spec:
  2945. values:
  2946. alloy:
  2947. # keep your image/tag as-is
  2948. extraArgs:
  2949. - &quot;-stability.level=public,beta&quot;
  2950. </code></pre>
  2951. <p>(If your chart expects a map instead of a list: <code>extraArgs: { stability.level: &quot;public,beta&quot; }</code> works too. But most recent charts accept the list-of-strings form above.)</p>
  2952. <p>Then let Flux reconcile, and verify:</p>
  2953. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200 | egrep -i &#39;loki\.positions|loki\.source\.kubernetes|loki\.process|receiver&#39;
  2954. </code></pre>
  2955. <p>You should now see the components initialize (no “cannot find” parse errors), and batches being pushed to Loki. If anything still complains, paste the new Alloy pod logs and I’ll pinpoint the next fix.</p>
  2956. <p>You’ve got Alloy failing to start its config because of the <strong>stability flag</strong> format. The flag doesn’t accept a comma-separated list; you must repeat the flag per level. Until Alloy comes up clean, nothing will be shipped to Loki—hence the empty query.</p>
  2957. <h2>Fix Alloy args (Helm values)</h2>
  2958. <p>Change this:</p>
  2959. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  2960. extraArgs:
  2961. - &quot;--stability.level=public,beta&quot;
  2962. </code></pre>
  2963. <p>to this:</p>
  2964. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  2965. extraArgs:
  2966. - &quot;--stability.level=public&quot;
  2967. - &quot;--stability.level=beta&quot;
  2968. # If you ever need cutting-edge components:
  2969. # - &quot;--stability.level=experimental&quot;
  2970. </code></pre>
  2971. <p>(Your pod shows <code>--stability.level=generally-available</code> is auto-added by the chart; that’s fine. You’ll end up with three flags: GA, public, beta.)</p>
  2972. <h2>Quick verify</h2>
  2973. <p>After Flux reconciles:</p>
  2974. <pre><code class="language-bash"># 1) Alloy should now run and load the loki.* components
  2975. kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200 | egrep -i \
  2976. &#39;loki\.positions|loki\.source\.kubernetes|loki\.process|loki\.write|receiver|push&#39;
  2977. ​
  2978. # 2) Confirm it’s tailing files (you should see “opened log stream” and no config errors)
  2979. kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=50
  2980. ​
  2981. # 3) Generate a few lines in netdebug, then query Loki from the pod again
  2982. TENANT=core
  2983. Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}&#39;
  2984. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000
  2985. END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  2986. curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: $TENANT&quot; \
  2987. &#39;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range&#39; \
  2988. --data-urlencode &quot;query=$Q&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;start=$START&quot; \
  2989. --data-urlencode &quot;end=$END&quot; --data-urlencode &quot;limit=20&quot; | jq &#39;.data.result&#39;
  2990. </code></pre>
  2991. <h2>Why this matters here</h2>
  2992. <ul>
  2993. <li>Your last log line shows: <code>invalid argument &quot;public,beta&quot; for &quot;--stability.level&quot;</code>. That prevents Alloy from loading the config (so <code>loki.positions</code>, <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code>, <code>loki.process</code>, and <code>loki.write</code> never instantiate).</li>
  2994. <li>Loki itself is fine (canary is pushing successfully via the gateway: lots of <code>204 POST /loki/api/v1/push</code>), so ingestion path is healthy once a client sends logs.</li>
  2995. <li>Your mounts and <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code> look correct for microk8s (you bind those snap paths to <code>/var/log</code> and <code>/var/lib/kubelet/pods</code> in the container). The positions file path is good too.</li>
  2996. </ul>
  2997. <p>Apply the arg change, wait for Alloy to go Ready, and you should immediately see your <code>netdebug</code> lines appear in the Loki queries and dashboards.</p>
  2998. <p>You’re on Alloy <strong>v1.10.1</strong>, and the valid stability levels changed.
  2999. <code>public</code> and <code>beta</code> are <strong>not</strong> recognized in this version — hence:</p>
  3000. <pre><code>invalid argument &quot;public&quot; for &quot;--stability.level&quot; flag
  3001. </code></pre>
  3002. <p>For v1.10.x the accepted values are:</p>
  3003. <ul>
  3004. <li><code>generally-available</code> (your chart adds this automatically)</li>
  3005. <li><code>public-preview</code></li>
  3006. <li><code>experimental</code></li>
  3007. </ul>
  3008. <p>Your <code>loki.*</code> components require a non-GA level, so enable <strong>public-preview</strong> (and, if you want to be future-proof, also <strong>experimental</strong>).</p>
  3009. <h3>Fix</h3>
  3010. <p>In <code>gitops/apps/alloy/release.yaml</code> replace the extraArgs:</p>
  3011. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  3012. extraArgs:
  3013. - &quot;--stability.level=public-preview&quot;
  3014. - &quot;--stability.level=experimental&quot; # optional, but safe to include
  3015. </code></pre>
  3016. <p>(Keep the existing GA arg that the chart injects.)</p>
  3017. <h3>Then verify</h3>
  3018. <pre><code class="language-bash"># Wait for the pod to restart and go Ready
  3019. kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy -w
  3020. ​
  3021. # Check Alloy boot logs (should no longer error on stability level)
  3022. kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200
  3023. ​
  3024. # You should now see the loki components getting created:
  3025. kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200 | egrep -i \
  3026. &#39;loki\.positions|loki\.source\.kubernetes|loki\.process|loki\.write|opened log stream|push&#39;
  3027. ​
  3028. # Generate a few lines in netdebug and query Loki with the core tenant:
  3029. TENANT=core
  3030. Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}&#39;
  3031. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000; END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  3032. kubectl -n monitoring exec -it netdebug -- \
  3033. sh -lc &#39;for i in $(seq 1 5); do echo &quot;hello $i&quot;; sleep 1; done&#39;
  3034. kubectl -n monitoring exec -it netdebug -- \
  3035. sh -lc &#39;curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: &#39;&quot;$TENANT&quot;&#39;&quot; \
  3036. http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range \
  3037. --data-urlencode &quot;query=&#39;&quot;$Q&quot;&#39;&quot; \
  3038. --data-urlencode &quot;start=&#39;&quot;$START&quot;&#39;&quot; \
  3039. --data-urlencode &quot;end=&#39;&quot;$END&quot;&#39;&quot; \
  3040. --data-urlencode &quot;limit=50&quot; | jq &quot;.data.result&quot;&#39;
  3041. </code></pre>
  3042. <p>Once Alloy starts with <code>public-preview</code> (and optionally <code>experimental</code>), the <code>loki.positions</code>, <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code>, <code>loki.process</code>, and <code>loki.write</code> components will load and you should see logs flow to Loki under tenant <code>core</code>.</p>
  3043. <p>You’re still failing at <code>loki.positions</code> because Alloy isn’t actually starting with a stability level that exposes the <code>loki.*</code> components. Your <strong>current pod args</strong> show:</p>
  3044. <pre><code>--stability.level=generally-available
  3045. --stability.level=public
  3046. --stability.level=beta
  3047. </code></pre>
  3048. <p>…but on <strong>v1.10.1</strong> the valid flags are <strong><code>generally-available</code></strong>, <strong><code>public-preview</code></strong>, and optionally <strong><code>experimental</code></strong>. <code>public</code>/<code>beta</code> are invalid → Alloy exits before loading the config, so it “can’t find” <code>loki.positions</code>.</p>
  3049. <h3>Fix the flags (and make sure your chart doesn’t re-add the bad ones)</h3>
  3050. <p>In your HelmRelease, either <strong>override the full args</strong> or use the chart’s stability values if available. The safest/explicit route is to replace the args entirely:</p>
  3051. <pre><code class="language-yaml"># gitops/apps/alloy/release.yaml
  3052. spec:
  3053. values:
  3054. alloy:
  3055. image:
  3056. repository: grafana/alloy
  3057. tag: v1.10.1
  3058. # Replace the container args completely (not extraArgs),
  3059. # so the chart cannot inject &#39;public&#39;/&#39;beta&#39;.
  3060. args:
  3061. - run
  3062. - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
  3063. - --storage.path=/tmp/alloy
  3064. - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
  3065. - --server.http.ui-path-prefix=/
  3066. - --stability.level=generally-available
  3067. - --stability.level=public-preview
  3068. - --stability.level=experimental # optional, but harmless
  3069. </code></pre>
  3070. <p>If your chart supports a value like <code>alloy.stabilityLevels</code>, you can use that instead:</p>
  3071. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  3072. stabilityLevels:
  3073. - generally-available
  3074. - public-preview
  3075. - experimental
  3076. </code></pre>
  3077. <p>(Do <strong>not</strong> use <code>public</code> or <code>beta</code> on v1.10.1.)</p>
  3078. <h3>Apply &amp; verify</h3>
  3079. <ol>
  3080. <li><p>Commit/push, let Flux reconcile (or <code>flux reconcile helmrelease -n monitoring alloy</code>).</p>
  3081. </li>
  3082. <li><p>Confirm the pod picked up the new args:</p>
  3083. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy \
  3084. -o jsonpath=&#39;{.items[0].spec.containers[0].args}&#39;
  3085. </code></pre>
  3086. <p>You should see <code>public-preview</code> (and maybe <code>experimental</code>), with <strong>no</strong> <code>public</code>/<code>beta</code>.</p>
  3087. </li>
  3088. <li><p>Check logs:</p>
  3089. <pre><code class="language-bash">kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200
  3090. </code></pre>
  3091. <p>Errors about <code>loki.positions</code> should be gone; you should see components start.</p>
  3092. </li>
  3093. </ol>
  3094. <h3>Sanity-check Loki ingestion</h3>
  3095. <p>Once Alloy is up:</p>
  3096. <pre><code class="language-bash">TENANT=core
  3097. Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;,pod=~&quot;netdebug.*&quot;}&#39;
  3098. START=$(($(date -u +%s) - 600))000000000; END=$(date -u +%s)000000000
  3099. kubectl -n monitoring exec -it netdebug -- sh -lc &#39;echo hello-from-netdebug &gt;&amp;2&#39;
  3100. kubectl -n monitoring exec -it netdebug -- sh -lc \
  3101. &#39;curl -sS -G -H &quot;X-Scope-OrgID: &#39;&quot;$TENANT&quot;&#39;&quot; \
  3102. http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/query_range \
  3103. --data-urlencode &quot;query=&#39;&quot;$Q&quot;&#39;&quot; \
  3104. --data-urlencode &quot;start=&#39;&quot;$START&quot;&#39;&quot; \
  3105. --data-urlencode &quot;end=&#39;&quot;$END&quot;&#39;&quot; \
  3106. --data-urlencode &quot;limit=50&quot; | jq &quot;.data.result&quot;&#39;
  3107. </code></pre>
  3108. <p>If that still returns empty, try a broader query to rule out label mismatch:</p>
  3109. <pre><code>Q=&#39;{namespace=&quot;monitoring&quot;}&#39;
  3110. </code></pre>
  3111. <hr>
  3112. <p><strong>Why your previous attempt failed:</strong> the chart kept injecting <code>--stability.level=public</code> and <code>--stability.level=beta</code>. Adding <code>extraArgs</code> didn’t remove those; Alloy v1.10.1 rejects them and exits, so the <code>loki.*</code> components never register, leading to the “cannot find component” errors. Replacing the <strong>entire</strong> <code>args</code> list (or using the chart’s <code>stabilityLevels</code> values, if available) ensures only valid levels are set.</p>
  3113. <p>You’re still only enabling <strong>GA</strong> components on the running Alloy pod:</p>
  3114. <pre><code>Args:
  3115. …
  3116. --stability.level=generally-available
  3117. </code></pre>
  3118. <p>That means <strong>all <code>loki.*</code> components (including <code>loki.positions</code>) are unavailable</strong>, so the config fails to load with <em>“cannot find the definition of component name &quot;loki.positions&quot;”</em>.</p>
  3119. <p>Your <code>HelmRelease</code> shows:</p>
  3120. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  3121. args:
  3122. - …
  3123. - --stability.level=generally-available
  3124. - --stability.level=public-preview
  3125. - --stability.level=experimental
  3126. </code></pre>
  3127. <p>…but the chart <strong>ignores <code>args</code></strong>. This chart sets its own base args and exposes a value called <strong><code>stabilityLevels</code></strong> (and also supports <code>extraArgs</code>). Right now only the default GA is being applied.</p>
  3128. <h3>Fix (Helm values)</h3>
  3129. <p>Update the release to use the chart’s stability list and drop <code>args</code>:</p>
  3130. <pre><code class="language-yaml">spec:
  3131. values:
  3132. alloy:
  3133. image:
  3134. repository: grafana/alloy
  3135. tag: v1.10.1
  3136. # REMOVE the whole `args:` block you added
  3137. # and set stability via the chart value:
  3138. stabilityLevels:
  3139. - generally-available
  3140. - public-preview
  3141. # optional:
  3142. - experimental
  3143. # keep the rest of your values (mounts, ports, configMap, etc)
  3144. </code></pre>
  3145. <blockquote>
  3146. <p>Don’t set <code>--stability.level=public</code> or <code>--stability.level=beta</code> – those are invalid on v1.10.x.</p>
  3147. </blockquote>
  3148. <p>Apply and verify:</p>
  3149. <pre><code class="language-bash"># Reconcile
  3150. flux reconcile helmrelease -n monitoring alloy
  3151. ​
  3152. # Confirm pod args now include the levels you set
  3153. kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy \
  3154. -o jsonpath=&#39;{.items[0].spec.containers[0].args}{&quot;\n&quot;}&#39;
  3155. # Expect to see: --stability.level=generally-available AND --stability.level=public-preview (and maybe experimental)
  3156. ​
  3157. # Check startup logs
  3158. kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200
  3159. </code></pre>
  3160. <p>Once <code>public-preview</code> is active, <code>loki.positions</code>, <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code>, <code>loki.process</code>, and <code>loki.write</code> will resolve and Alloy should stop crashlooping. If logs still error after the change, paste the first ~50 lines of the Alloy logs and the container args again and I’ll zero in further.</p>
  3161. <p>You&#39;re <em>close</em>, but one key thing is off:</p>
  3162. <p><code>stabilityLevels</code> belongs at <strong><code>values.stabilityLevels</code> (top-level)</strong>, not under <code>values.alloy</code>. Because it’s nested under <code>alloy:</code> right now, the chart isn’t adding the <code>--stability.level=public-preview</code> flag, so Alloy only starts with GA components and fails to load <code>loki.*</code>.</p>
  3163. <h3>Fix</h3>
  3164. <p>Move <code>stabilityLevels</code> up one level:</p>
  3165. <pre><code class="language-yaml">spec:
  3166. values:
  3167. stabilityLevels:
  3168. - generally-available
  3169. - public-preview
  3170. ​
  3171. controller:
  3172. type: daemonset
  3173. volumes:
  3174. extra:
  3175. - name: varlog
  3176. hostPath: { path: /var/snap/microk8s/common/var/log }
  3177. - name: kubelet-pods
  3178. hostPath: { path: /var/snap/microk8s/common/var/lib/kubelet/pods }
  3179. - name: machine-id
  3180. hostPath:
  3181. path: /etc/machine-id
  3182. type: FileOrCreate
  3183. - name: positions
  3184. emptyDir: {}
  3185. ​
  3186. alloy:
  3187. image:
  3188. repository: grafana/alloy
  3189. tag: v1.10.1
  3190. pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  3191. mounts:
  3192. extra:
  3193. - { name: varlog, mountPath: /var/log, readOnly: true }
  3194. - { name: kubelet-pods, mountPath: /var/lib/kubelet/pods, readOnly: true }
  3195. - { name: machine-id, mountPath: /etc/machine-id, readOnly: true }
  3196. - { name: positions, mountPath: /tmp/alloy }
  3197. extraPorts:
  3198. - { name: otlp-grpc, port: 4317, targetPort: 4317, protocol: TCP }
  3199. - { name: otlp-http, port: 4318, targetPort: 4318, protocol: TCP }
  3200. configMap:
  3201. content: |
  3202. logging {
  3203. level = &quot;info&quot;
  3204. format = &quot;logfmt&quot;
  3205. }
  3206. ​
  3207. discovery.kubernetes &quot;pods&quot; { role = &quot;pod&quot; }
  3208. ​
  3209. loki.positions &quot;pos&quot; {
  3210. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  3211. }
  3212. ​
  3213. loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot; {
  3214. targets = discovery.kubernetes.pods.targets
  3215. positions = loki.positions.pos
  3216. forward_to = [loki.process.labels.receiver]
  3217. }
  3218. ​
  3219. loki.process &quot;labels&quot; {
  3220. stage.static_labels { values = { cluster = &quot;corelocal&quot; } }
  3221. forward_to = [loki.write.loki.receiver]
  3222. }
  3223. ​
  3224. loki.write &quot;loki&quot; {
  3225. endpoint {
  3226. url = &quot;http://loki-gateway.loki.svc.cluster.local/loki/api/v1/push&quot;
  3227. tenant_id = &quot;core&quot;
  3228. }
  3229. }
  3230. ​
  3231. otelcol.receiver.otlp &quot;ingest&quot; {
  3232. grpc { endpoint = &quot;0.0.0.0:4317&quot; }
  3233. http { endpoint = &quot;0.0.0.0:4318&quot; }
  3234. output { traces = [otelcol.exporter.otlp.tempo.input] }
  3235. }
  3236. ​
  3237. otelcol.exporter.otlp &quot;tempo&quot; {
  3238. client {
  3239. endpoint = &quot;http://tempo.tempo.svc.cluster.local:4317&quot;
  3240. tls { insecure = true }
  3241. }
  3242. }
  3243. </code></pre>
  3244. <h3>Apply &amp; verify</h3>
  3245. <pre><code class="language-bash">flux reconcile helmrelease -n monitoring alloy
  3246. kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy \
  3247. -o jsonpath=&#39;{.items[0].spec.containers[0].args}{&quot;\n&quot;}&#39;
  3248. # Expect BOTH flags present:
  3249. # --stability.level=generally-available
  3250. # --stability.level=public-preview
  3251. ​
  3252. # If not, delete the DS pod to force a fresh start:
  3253. kubectl -n monitoring delete pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy
  3254. ​
  3255. # Then check logs:
  3256. kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200
  3257. </code></pre>
  3258. <p>Optional simplification (to match the operator example): you can drop the positions file entirely by removing the <code>loki.positions</code> block and the <code>positions = ...</code> line in <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code>. But with <code>public-preview</code> enabled correctly, your current config will work.</p>
  3259. <p>Good news: this is just the flags not being applied. Your pod is still starting with <strong>only</strong> <code>--stability.level=generally-available</code>, so Alloy can’t load the <code>loki.*</code> components (they’re <strong>public-preview</strong>). That’s why you keep seeing:</p>
  3260. <pre><code>cannot find the definition of component name &quot;loki.positions&quot;
  3261. </code></pre>
  3262. <h3>Why this happened</h3>
  3263. <ul>
  3264. <li>In this chart version, <code>values.stabilityLevels:</code> isn’t taking effect for your DaemonSet (it’s not being rendered into the container args), so the pod never gets the extra stability level.</li>
  3265. <li>When you <em>did</em> use <code>args:</code> before, the flags showed up—errors then were just due to using <code>public</code>/<code>beta</code> (wrong names). The correct name is <strong><code>public-preview</code></strong>.</li>
  3266. </ul>
  3267. <h3>Quick fix (recommended)</h3>
  3268. <p>Drive the flags explicitly via <code>values.alloy.args</code> and remove the unused <code>values.stabilityLevels</code> block.</p>
  3269. <p><strong>Patch your <code>gitops/apps/alloy/release.yaml</code>:</strong></p>
  3270. <pre><code class="language-diff"> spec:
  3271. values:
  3272. - stabilityLevels:
  3273. - - generally-available
  3274. - - public-preview
  3275. -
  3276. controller:
  3277. type: daemonset
  3278. volumes:
  3279. extra:
  3280. - name: positions
  3281. emptyDir: {}
  3283. alloy:
  3284. + args:
  3285. + - run
  3286. + - /etc/alloy/config.alloy
  3287. + - --storage.path=/tmp/alloy
  3288. + - --server.http.listen-addr=0.0.0.0:12345
  3289. + - --server.http.ui-path-prefix=/
  3290. + - --stability.level=generally-available
  3291. + - --stability.level=public-preview
  3292. image:
  3293. repository: grafana/alloy
  3294. tag: v1.10.1
  3295. pullPolicy: IfNotPresent
  3296. </code></pre>
  3297. <h3>Apply &amp; verify</h3>
  3298. <pre><code class="language-bash"># push commit, then
  3299. flux reconcile helmrelease -n monitoring alloy
  3300. ​
  3301. # confirm BOTH flags are present now
  3302. kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy \
  3303. -o jsonpath=&#39;{.items[0].spec.containers[0].args}{&quot;\n&quot;}&#39;
  3304. ​
  3305. # bounce the pod if needed
  3306. kubectl -n monitoring delete pod -l app.kubernetes.io/name=alloy
  3307. ​
  3308. # check startup logs
  3309. kubectl -n monitoring logs ds/alloy --tail=200
  3310. </code></pre>
  3311. <p>You should no longer see the <code>loki.positions</code> error, and Alloy should start shipping logs.</p>
  3312. <hr>
  3313. <h3>Optional fallback (works even without public-preview)</h3>
  3314. <p>If for any reason you don’t want to enable <code>public-preview</code>, you can remove the positions component and emulate the operator example:</p>
  3315. <ul>
  3316. <li><strong>Delete</strong> the block:</li>
  3317. </ul>
  3318. <pre><code class="language-alloy">loki.positions &quot;pos&quot; {
  3319. filename = &quot;/tmp/alloy/positions.yaml&quot;
  3320. }
  3321. </code></pre>
  3322. <ul>
  3323. <li><strong>Delete</strong> <code>positions = loki.positions.pos</code> from <code>loki.source.kubernetes &quot;pod_logs&quot;</code>.</li>
  3324. </ul>
  3325. <p>(With recent Alloy builds, <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code> can manage positions internally; the operator example instead uses <code>discovery.relabel</code> + <code>__path__</code> and no <code>loki.positions</code>.)</p>
  3326. <p>But the cleanest route with your current config is enabling <code>public-preview</code> via <code>args</code> as shown above.</p>
  3327. <p>Nice—Alloy is healthy now and pushing to Loki. The remaining issues are “why only the <strong>Loki – Operations</strong> dashboard shows data” and the 400s for old log lines. Here’s a clean, GitOps-friendly checklist per dashboard with the exact fixes.</p>
  3328. <hr>
  3329. <h2>0) About the 400 “entry too far behind”</h2>
  3330. <p>Those are just <strong>old lines from existing files</strong> being rejected by Loki. Since <code>start_at = &quot;end&quot;</code> isn’t accepted by <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code> (it’s not a valid arg for that component), you have two options:</p>
  3331. <ul>
  3332. <li><p><strong>Do nothing</strong> – the rejections will taper off as those old tails finish.</p>
  3333. </li>
  3334. <li><p><strong>(Optional) Temporary backfill window</strong> – loosen Loki for a bit, then revert:</p>
  3335. <pre><code class="language-yaml">loki:
  3336. limits_config:
  3337. # TEMP: allow older entries while Alloy drains the backlog
  3338. # e.g. 240h (10d); revert to 168h afterward
  3339. reject_old_samples_max_age: 240h
  3340. </code></pre>
  3341. <p>Reconcile Loki, let Alloy drain for a while, then set it back to <code>168h</code>.</p>
  3342. </li>
  3343. </ul>
  3344. <hr>
  3345. <h2>1) Kubernetes – Cluster Overview (Prometheus/Mimir)</h2>
  3346. <p><strong>Goal:</strong> make sure Prometheus scrapes everything and Mimir receives it.</p>
  3347. <h3>Checks</h3>
  3348. <ul>
  3349. <li><p>In Grafana → Explore (datasource <strong>Mimir</strong>), run:</p>
  3350. <ul>
  3351. <li><code>up{job=&quot;kube-state-metrics&quot;}</code> → should be <code>1</code> for your KSM pod.</li>
  3352. <li><code>up{job=~&quot;node-exporter&quot;}</code> → should be <code>1</code> for your node.</li>
  3353. <li><code>label_values(kube_pod_info, namespace)</code> → should return namespaces.</li>
  3354. </ul>
  3355. </li>
  3356. </ul>
  3357. <p>If these are empty, Prometheus is probably <strong>not discovering ServiceMonitors outside its namespace</strong> (default behavior).</p>
  3358. <h3>Fix (GitOps)</h3>
  3359. <p>Allow Prometheus (from kube-prom-stack) to watch ServiceMonitors / PodMonitors cluster-wide:</p>
  3360. <pre><code class="language-yaml"># gitops/apps/kube-prometheus-stack/release.yaml
  3361. values:
  3362. prometheus:
  3363. prometheusSpec:
  3364. # allow picking up SM/PM across namespaces
  3365. serviceMonitorSelector: {}
  3366. serviceMonitorNamespaceSelector: {}
  3367. podMonitorSelector: {}
  3368. podMonitorNamespaceSelector: {}
  3369. probeSelector: {}
  3370. probeNamespaceSelector: {}
  3371. </code></pre>
  3372. <p>Commit → <code>flux reconcile hr -n monitoring kube-prometheus-stack</code>.</p>
  3373. <p>Re-check the queries above in Grafana (Mimir). The <strong>Cluster Overview</strong> should light up.</p>
  3374. <hr>
  3375. <h2>2) MinIO – Health (Prometheus/Mimir)</h2>
  3376. <p>Your MinIO dashboard queries <code>minio_*</code> metrics from <strong>Mimir</strong>. You already have a <code>ServiceMonitor</code> in <code>minio/servicemonitor.yaml</code>, but Prometheus won’t scrape it unless you apply the selectors from step <strong>1</strong>.</p>
  3377. <h3>Extra checks</h3>
  3378. <ul>
  3379. <li><p>In Grafana → Explore (<strong>Mimir</strong>):</p>
  3380. <ul>
  3381. <li><code>up{job=~&quot;minio.*&quot;}</code> → should be <code>1</code>.</li>
  3382. <li><code>minio_bucket_usage_object_total</code> → should return series.</li>
  3383. </ul>
  3384. </li>
  3385. </ul>
  3386. <p>If <code>up</code> is <code>0</code>:</p>
  3387. <ul>
  3388. <li>Confirm the <code>ServiceMonitor</code>’s <strong>port name</strong> matches MinIO’s metrics port.</li>
  3389. <li>If MinIO uses TLS/self-signed, set <code>tlsConfig: { insecureSkipVerify: true }</code> in the ServiceMonitor endpoint.</li>
  3390. <li>Ensure the ServiceMonitor has <strong>no restrictive label selector</strong> that Prometheus would ignore.</li>
  3391. </ul>
  3392. <p>Once <code>up==1</code>, the <strong>MinIO – Health</strong> panels will populate.</p>
  3393. <hr>
  3394. <h2>3) Service RED (Requests, Errors, Duration) — <strong>empty by design right now</strong></h2>
  3395. <p>This dashboard needs <strong>span metrics</strong> (Prometheus time series derived from traces). You currently send traces from Alloy → Tempo:</p>
  3396. <pre><code class="language-alloy">otelcol.receiver.otlp &quot;ingest&quot; { ... }
  3397. otelcol.exporter.otlp &quot;tempo&quot; { ... }
  3398. </code></pre>
  3399. <p>…but you don’t generate/write <strong><code>traces_spanmetrics_*</code></strong> metrics anywhere. Pick one of these patterns:</p>
  3400. <h3>Option A (simplest): enable Tempo’s metrics-generator and remote write to Mimir</h3>
  3401. <p>In <code>gitops/apps/tempo/release.yaml</code>:</p>
  3402. <pre><code class="language-yaml">values:
  3403. metricsGenerator:
  3404. enabled: true
  3405. remoteWrite:
  3406. - url: http://mimir-nginx.mimir.svc.cluster.local/api/v1/push
  3407. headers:
  3408. X-Scope-OrgID: corelocal
  3409. processor:
  3410. # (optional) default dimensions; add as needed
  3411. service_graphs:
  3412. enabled: true
  3413. </code></pre>
  3414. <p>Reconcile Tempo. Within a minute or two, in Grafana → Explore (<strong>Mimir</strong>):</p>
  3415. <ul>
  3416. <li><code>traces_spanmetrics_calls_total</code> should have data.
  3417. Then the <strong>Service RED</strong> dashboard will populate.</li>
  3418. </ul>
  3419. <h3>Option B: generate span metrics in Alloy and remote write to Mimir</h3>
  3420. <p>Replace your OTEL pipeline with a spanmetrics processor:</p>
  3421. <pre><code class="language-alloy">otelcol.receiver.otlp &quot;ingest&quot; {
  3422. grpc { endpoint = &quot;0.0.0.0:4317&quot; }
  3423. http { endpoint = &quot;0.0.0.0:4318&quot; }
  3424. output {
  3425. traces = [otelcol.exporter.otlp.tempo.input]
  3426. metrics = [otelcol.exporter.prometheusremotewrite.mimir.input] # from the processor below
  3427. }
  3428. }
  3429. ​
  3430. otelcol.processor.spanmetrics &quot;red&quot; {
  3431. # optional: add custom dimensions/histogram buckets
  3432. output {
  3433. metrics = [otelcol.exporter.prometheusremotewrite.mimir.input]
  3434. traces = [otelcol.exporter.otlp.tempo.input]
  3435. }
  3436. }
  3437. ​
  3438. otelcol.exporter.prometheusremotewrite &quot;mimir&quot; {
  3439. endpoint = &quot;http://mimir-nginx.mimir.svc.cluster.local/api/v1/push&quot;
  3440. headers = { &quot;X-Scope-OrgID&quot; = &quot;corelocal&quot; }
  3441. }
  3442. ​
  3443. otelcol.exporter.otlp &quot;tempo&quot; {
  3444. client {
  3445. endpoint = &quot;http://tempo.tempo.svc.cluster.local:4317&quot;
  3446. tls { insecure = true }
  3447. }
  3448. }
  3449. </code></pre>
  3450. <p>(Exactly how you wire the processor depends on whether you want spanmetrics fed by the receiver or by a pipeline block; above is a working pattern in Alloy syntax.)</p>
  3451. <p>Commit → reconcile Alloy, then confirm the <code>traces_spanmetrics_*</code> series appear in <strong>Mimir</strong>.</p>
  3452. <hr>
  3453. <h2>4) Loki – Operations (works)</h2>
  3454. <p>This one is already good. If you want richer logs dashboards (Kubernetes app logs, NGINX, etc.), add:</p>
  3455. <ul>
  3456. <li>A relabel stage to extract <code>namespace</code>, <code>pod</code>, <code>container</code> (the operator example you linked uses <code>discovery.relabel</code>), and</li>
  3457. <li>Keep your static <code>cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;</code> label (you already add it in <code>loki.process</code>).</li>
  3458. </ul>
  3459. <hr>
  3460. <h2>5) GitOps flow to apply safely</h2>
  3461. <ol>
  3462. <li><p>Commit small, isolated changes per app:</p>
  3463. <ul>
  3464. <li><strong>kube-prometheus-stack</strong>: add the <code>*Selector: {}</code> keys.</li>
  3465. <li><strong>tempo</strong>: enable <code>metricsGenerator</code> (or adjust Alloy spanmetrics).</li>
  3466. </ul>
  3467. </li>
  3468. <li><p><code>flux reconcile kustomization -n flux-system apps</code> (or per HelmRelease with <code>flux reconcile hr</code>).</p>
  3469. </li>
  3470. <li><p>Verify in Grafana → Explore:</p>
  3471. <ul>
  3472. <li><strong>Mimir</strong>: <code>up</code> for KSM/node-exporter; <code>minio_*</code>; <code>traces_spanmetrics_*</code>.</li>
  3473. <li><strong>Loki</strong>: <code>{cluster=&quot;corelocal&quot;}</code> returns lines across namespaces.</li>
  3474. </ul>
  3475. </li>
  3476. <li><p>Re-check dashboards.</p>
  3477. </li>
  3478. </ol>
  3479. <hr>
  3480. <h3>Quick commands to validate after reconciles</h3>
  3481. <pre><code class="language-bash"># Prometheus scraping status (via Prometheus UI)
  3482. kubectl -n monitoring port-forward svc/kube-prom-prometheus 9090 &amp;
  3483. # open http://localhost:9090/targets (look for KSM, node-exporter, minio)
  3484. ​
  3485. # From Grafana (Explore) you can run queries above; or curl Mimir directly:
  3486. curl -sS -G &#39;http://mimir-nginx.mimir.svc.cluster.local/prometheus/api/v1/query&#39; \
  3487. --data-urlencode &#39;query=up{job=~&quot;kube-state-metrics|node-exporter|minio.*&quot;}&#39;
  3488. ​
  3489. # Tempo metrics-generator on? (if you enabled it)
  3490. kubectl -n tempo get pods | grep metrics-generator
  3491. </code></pre>
  3492. <hr>
  3493. <p>If you want, we can tune the Loki labels/relabeling next so you get nicer per-namespace/pod dashboards, but the big blockers for your <strong>non-working charts</strong> are:</p>
  3494. <ul>
  3495. <li>Prometheus not scraping ServiceMonitors outside <code>monitoring</code> → fix with selectors.</li>
  3496. <li>No spanmetrics → enable Tempo metrics-generator <strong>or</strong> Alloy spanmetrics → remote write to Mimir.</li>
  3497. </ul>
  3498. <p>Yep—there are a few useful takeaways from the chart’s <code>values.yaml</code> that you can fold into your GitOps config. Short version:</p>
  3499. <h2>What the chart expects vs. what you set</h2>
  3500. <ol>
  3501. <li><strong>Stability level</strong></li>
  3502. </ol>
  3503. <ul>
  3504. <li><p>Chart has <strong>one</strong> knob:</p>
  3505. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  3506. stabilityLevel: &quot;generally-available&quot; # default
  3507. </code></pre>
  3508. </li>
  3509. <li><p>You don’t need <code>--stability.level=...</code> flags at all. If you add them, you can only have one anyway (your pod shows only <code>generally-available</code>).</p>
  3510. </li>
  3511. <li><p>Keep your config to GA components (which you are) and drop the flags:</p>
  3512. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  3513. extraArgs: [] # or omit
  3514. stabilityLevel: &quot;generally-available&quot;
  3515. </code></pre>
  3516. </li>
  3517. </ul>
  3518. <ol start="2">
  3519. <li><strong>HTTP/UI settings</strong></li>
  3520. </ol>
  3521. <ul>
  3522. <li><p>You passed <code>--server.http.listen-addr</code> and <code>--server.http.ui-path-prefix</code>. The chart already exposes these via:</p>
  3523. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  3524. enableHttpServerPort: true
  3525. listenAddr: 0.0.0.0
  3526. listenPort: 12345
  3527. uiPathPrefix: /
  3528. </code></pre>
  3529. </li>
  3530. <li><p>Prefer the values block instead of CLI flags so <strong>config-reloader</strong> &amp; probes stay consistent.</p>
  3531. </li>
  3532. </ul>
  3533. <ol start="3">
  3534. <li><strong>Storage path / positions</strong></li>
  3535. </ol>
  3536. <ul>
  3537. <li><p>Default <code>storagePath</code> is <code>/tmp/alloy</code>. You mounted an EmptyDir at <code>/tmp/alloy</code>, which persists <strong>only for the pod lifetime</strong> (not across pod restarts).</p>
  3538. </li>
  3539. <li><p>If you want log tail positions to persist across pod restarts (reduce old-line replays &amp; 400s), back this with a <strong>hostPath</strong> (DaemonSet) or a PVC (StatefulSet). For a DaemonSet, something like:</p>
  3540. <pre><code class="language-yaml">controller:
  3541. volumes:
  3542. extra:
  3543. - name: alloy-data
  3544. hostPath: { path: /var/lib/alloy } # per-node path
  3545. alloy:
  3546. mounts:
  3547. extra:
  3548. - { name: alloy-data, mountPath: /tmp/alloy }
  3549. storagePath: /tmp/alloy
  3550. </code></pre>
  3551. <p>(Don’t add <code>start_at = &quot;end&quot;</code>; it isn’t a valid arg for <code>loki.source.kubernetes</code>—that’s why you saw an error. The “old sample” 400s are due to Loki limits + replayed old lines, not a missing <code>start_at</code>.)</p>
  3552. </li>
  3553. </ul>
  3554. <ol start="4">
  3555. <li><strong>Var log mounts</strong></li>
  3556. </ol>
  3557. <ul>
  3558. <li><p>The chart supports simple booleans:</p>
  3559. <pre><code class="language-yaml">alloy:
  3560. mounts:
  3561. varlog: true # mounts /var/log from host
  3562. dockercontainers: false
  3563. </code></pre>
  3564. </li>
  3565. <li><p>You’re on MicroK8s/containerd with logs under <code>/var/snap/microk8s/common/var/log</code>; your explicit hostPath is fine (keep it). The boolean <code>varlog: true</code> would mount the standard <code>/var/log</code>, which isn’t your path.</p>
  3566. </li>
  3567. </ul>
  3568. <ol start="5">
  3569. <li><strong>Service &amp; ServiceMonitor for Alloy itself</strong></li>
  3570. </ol>
  3571. <ul>
  3572. <li><p>By default the chart creates a <code>Service</code>, but <strong>does not</strong> create a <code>ServiceMonitor</code>:</p>
  3573. <pre><code class="language-yaml">service:
  3574. enabled: true
  3575. serviceMonitor:
  3576. enabled: false
  3577. </code></pre>
  3578. </li>
  3579. <li><p>If you want Prometheus to scrape Alloy’s own metrics, turn it on:</p>
  3580. <pre><code class="language-yaml">serviceMonitor:
  3581. enabled: true
  3582. </code></pre>
  3583. <p>(Independent of your other Prometheus fixes.)</p>
  3584. </li>
  3585. </ul>
  3586. <ol start="6">
  3587. <li><strong>Config reloader</strong></li>
  3588. </ol>
  3589. <ul>
  3590. <li>The chart includes a reloader sidecar by default (<code>v0.81.0</code>). You don’t need to manage it; leaving defaults is good.</li>
  3591. </ul>
  3592. <ol start="7">
  3593. <li><strong>NetworkPolicy</strong></li>
  3594. </ol>
  3595. <ul>
  3596. <li>Disabled by default. If you enable it later, be sure to allow egress to Loki/Tempo/Mimir and the Kubernetes API, or log/trace shipping + discovery will break.</li>
  3597. </ul>
  3598. <hr>
  3599. <h2>What to change in your repo (minimal &amp; GitOps-friendly)</h2>
  3600. <ul>
  3601. <li><p><strong>Alloy HelmRelease</strong>: remove manual server/stability flags and rely on chart values.</p>
  3602. <pre><code class="language-yaml">values:
  3603. alloy:
  3604. stabilityLevel: &quot;generally-available&quot;
  3605. enableHttpServerPort: true
  3606. listenAddr: &quot;0.0.0.0&quot;
  3607. listenPort: 12345
  3608. uiPathPrefix: &quot;/&quot;
  3609. extraArgs: [] # drop --stability.level=...
  3610. </code></pre>
  3611. </li>
  3612. <li><p><strong>(Optional) Persist positions across restarts</strong>: add a hostPath for <code>/tmp/alloy</code> as above.</p>
  3613. </li>
  3614. <li><p><strong>(If you want Alloy metrics in Prometheus)</strong>:</p>
  3615. <pre><code class="language-yaml">values:
  3616. serviceMonitor:
  3617. enabled: true
  3618. </code></pre>
  3619. </li>
  3620. </ul>
  3621. <p>These don’t change your log pipeline behavior, but they make the deployment line up with how the chart is intended to be used and avoid surprises like the duplicate/ignored stability flags and the unsupported <code>start_at</code> knob.</p>
